Verified research findings (143)

items: [A | guideline supported] The KDIGO 2026 anemia guideline uses TSAT and ferritin thresholds to guide iron therapy and recommends addressing correctable causes of anemia before using an ESA or HIF-PHI. It also recommends individualized Hb thresholds for starting an ESA. - PMID:41485807, PMID:42735412

[A | guideline supported] KDIGO 2026 recommends an upper hemoglobin target below 11.5 g/dL (<115 g/L) during ESA maintenance therapy. Hb thresholds for ESA initiation are individualized to patient characteristics, symptoms and values. - PMID:42735412

[A | guideline supported] KDIGO 2026 recommends the following sequence: address correctable causes of anemia before using an ESA or HIF-PHI; use transferrin saturation and ferritin thresholds to guide iron therapy; prefer IV iron in hemodialysis; and use an ESA rather than a HIF-PHI first line. - PMID:42735412

[B | guideline supported] An international guideline states that relatives with heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants should only be considered as a last resort for living kidney donation. A review strongly recommends genetic testing of at-risk potential donors before transplantation because carriers have an inherent kidney disease risk that may worsen after nephrectomy. - PMID:39558650, PMID:39673454

[B | evidence supported] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome, mutation type predicts age at kidney failure. Truncating-type variants had a mean ESRF age of 19.8 years. Non-glycine or 3' glycine missense variants had a mean of 25.7 years, and 5' glycine substitutions had a later mean of 30.1 years. Phenotype within a family was very consistent. - PMID:12105244

[B | evidence supported] In South Asian adults, creatinine-based eGFR equations overestimated measured GFR. All equations performed below the accepted 75% P30 accuracy threshold, and age, sex, ethnicity and cohort type modified bias. - PMID:41550526

[B | evidence supported] Within the same South Asian systematic review, cystatin C-based equations showed the least bias. Combined creatinine–cystatin C equations achieved the best accuracy, the only group with P30 reaching about 79–82%. - PMID:41550526

[B | evidence supported] In a meta-analysis of general-population and CKD cohorts, cystatin C alone or combined with creatinine strengthened the association between eGFR and death and end-stage renal disease. Results were similar in CKD cohorts. - PMID:24004120

[B | evidence supported] In the 2021 race-free CKD-EPI development and validation work, creatinine–cystatin C equations were more accurate than creatinine-only equations. The new creatinine-only equation overestimated measured GFR in non-Black participants. - PMID:34554658

[B | guideline supported] A UK practice guideline states that iron deficiency and EPO deficiency are the most common causes of anemia in CKD, especially in people requiring kidney replacement therapy. - PMID:40240983

[B | evidence supported] In a systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 studies in CKD patients, each 1% increase in RDW was associated with higher all-cause mortality. The association held in the hemodialysis subgroup and when RDW was analysed categorically. - PMID:28916240

[B | evidence supported] In a non-dialysis CKD cohort, RDW was the only CBC-derived marker that stayed independently associated with all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment. Once RDW was elevated, NLR added no further prognostic information. The abstract does not report an RDW-specific estimate for dialysis initiation. - PMID:42329902

[B | guideline supported] The 2024 ERKNet/ERA/ESPN Alport guideline recommends that relatives carrying heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants be considered only as the last possible resource for living kidney donation. This constrains living-donor selection from maternal-line female relatives in an X-linked pedigree. - PMID:39673454

[B | guideline supported] The 2024 ERKNet/ERA/ESPN Alport guideline states that relatives with heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants should only be considered as a last-resort living kidney donor. This is a recommendation rather than reported long-term donor outcome data. - PMID:39673454

[C | evidence supported] In Alport syndrome, defects in the COL4A3/A4/A5 type IV collagen network disrupt the glomerular basement membrane. This lets red cells and albumin leak into the urine and drives inflammation, fibrosis and loss of kidney function. This is the likely mechanism behind this patient's hematuria, proteinuria and markedly raised creatinine. - PMID:35806283

[C | evidence supported] Serum creatinine and albuminuria are late markers in Alport syndrome. A creatinine this high therefore indicates advanced, already established loss of kidney function rather than early injury. - PMID:35806283

[C | emerging] In an Alport cohort, rapid eGFR decline was defined as a loss of more than 6 mL/min/1.73m2 per year. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) was independently associated with yearly eGFR loss, and urinary IgG was the most sensitive marker for identifying decline. This patient's two-point slope (about -36.5 mL/min/1.73m2 per year, creatinine 4.13 to 10.85 mg/dL in about 4.5 months) far exceeds that definition. - PMID:42415835

[C | evidence supported] Creatinine is secreted by renal tubular transporters (OCT2, MATE1/2-K). Drugs that inhibit these transporters, such as trimethoprim, cimetidine, pyrimethamine, dolutegravir, cobicistat, dronedarone and some tyrosine kinase inhibitors, can raise serum creatinine without any change in kidney function. Such rises can mimic AKI criteria. - PMID:36859345

[C | evidence supported] Serum creatinine depends on muscle mass and nutritional status. It falls with undernutrition and muscle wasting, so normal or modestly raised values can mask renal dysfunction. The creatinine-to-cystatin C ratio is used as a muscle-mass (sarcopenia) marker, which shows that cystatin C is less affected by muscle than creatinine. - PMID:22349551, PMID:40506715, PMID:42739085

[C | emerging] Related tests in Alport syndrome include quantified proteinuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine or protein-to-creatinine ratio) and assessment of persistent hematuria. Cascade screening of first-degree relatives effectively identifies relatives with ongoing or at-risk kidney disease. - PMID:38117295, PMID:42529192

[C | emerging] In a retrospective cohort of 534 maintenance hemodialysis patients, serum potassium was among the independent predictors of all-cause mortality on multivariate analysis. The abstract does not report the direction of the association or a threshold. - PMID:42947841

[C | hypothesis] Low-sodium salt substitutes are mainly a mixture of sodium chloride and potassium chloride, so they are a source of dietary potassium. The guideline abstract does not address their use in advanced CKD. - PMID:38923391

[C | evidence supported] Thiazide diuretics lower serum potassium in a dose-dependent manner. Diuretic exposure is therefore a potential confounder of potassium interpretation, which cannot be assessed here because medication reconciliation is unknown. - PMID:3306212, PMID:8876478

[C | emerging] RDW is described as a low-cost haematological indicator reflecting systemic inflammation and nutritional status. This is the only mechanistic framing in the sources; no source addresses CKD-related anaemia mechanisms. - PMID:41973375

[C | emerging] In a weighted NHANES cohort of 17,412 low-income US adults, higher RDW was associated with all-cause mortality. Each 1% increase carried an 11% higher adjusted risk. The relationship was nonlinear, with an inflection at 15.9% above which the association was no longer significant. - PMID:42948113

[C | emerging] Elevated RDW is independently associated with adverse outcomes in several diseases: colorectal cancer survival, multiple myeloma survival, 12-month MACE in HFpEF, and in-hospital mortality in ACS. RDW-SD may carry stronger prognostic information than RDW-CV. - PMID:41246322, PMID:41973375, PMID:42940108

[C | evidence supported] Used alone, RDW discriminates outcomes poorly and should not be used as a standalone prognostic tool. Standardised thresholds and measurement timing are lacking. - PMID:41973375, PMID:42940108

[C | evidence supported] Genetic testing of COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 by next-generation sequencing is described as allowing accurate diagnosis of Alport syndrome. A consensus classification frames collagen IV α345 disorders around regular monitoring and early treatment. - PMID:29551517, PMID:35806283

[C | evidence supported] Expression of collagen IV chains in skin and kidney basement membranes is described as allowing diagnosis and determination of the mode of transmission in most patients. - PMID:27816395

[C | emerging] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome, maintained diffuse glomerular α3(IV) collagen staining was associated with later onset of proteinuria and later decline to eGFR <90. Segmental or absent staining was linked to null or truncating COL4A5 variants. - PMID:23371956

[C | emerging] Kidney transcriptome sequencing identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, including splice-altering variants not readily resolved by DNA sequencing. Its role in diagnosing the Alport spectrum is emerging. - PMID:42614610

[C | evidence supported] Albuminuria and serum creatinine are the conventional biomarkers in Alport syndrome but increase relatively late. In a retrospective cohort, UACR was independently associated with yearly eGFR loss after adjustment for confounders. - PMID:35806283, PMID:42415835

[C | evidence supported] Spot-urine UACR and UPCR were reliable alternatives to 24-hour collection in children with early Alport syndrome. UPCR substantially exceeded UACR at the earliest stage, suggesting UPCR is informative early. - PMID:37174733

[C | emerging] Urinary IgG had the highest sensitivity for identifying kidney function decline in one cohort. The authors propose combining it with albuminuria pending external validation. - PMID:42415835

[C | emerging] A urinary peptidomic classifier based on CE-MS (mostly collagen-derived peptides) showed very high diagnostic accuracy for pediatric Alport syndrome in internal validation. It may complement genetic testing. - PMID:42927079

[C | evidence supported] Cascade screening of at-risk relatives combines kidney function, urinalysis or proteinuria testing and testing for the familial COL4 variant. It is described as effective for identifying affected relatives. - PMID:42529192

[C | evidence supported] Serum cystatin C is described as a well-established, early and accurate CKD biomarker. It is particularly useful when creatinine is an inadequate marker, while the limitations of creatinine are well documented. Generalisable use requires assays and eGFR equations standardised to the International Standard. - PMID:32450046

[C | emerging] In acute deterioration on established CKD, creatinine-based definitions show reduced prognostic accuracy. Cystatin C-based eGFR is reported to discriminate mortality and progression better. Definitions of acute-on-chronic kidney disease are heterogeneous. - PMID:42954720

[C | emerging] Most biomarkers used in acute-on-chronic kidney injury were identified in isolated AKI and have not been specifically studied in CKD. Acute-on-chronic injury is associated with higher mortality, greater need for kidney replacement therapy and lower recovery. - PMID:42757157

[C | emerging] Plasma TNFR1, TNFR2 and KIM-1, and urinary MCP-1 and EGF, are the most studied prognostic CKD biomarkers. Plasma WFDC2, MMP-7, EFNA4 and EPHA2 are newer candidates. Data on biomarkers that predict treatment response are scarce. One review judges that some biomarkers may have enough data for clinical implementation. - PMID:34475336

[C | emerging] Among 37 urinary biomarkers (53 studies), KIM-1 performed best for diagnosis of incident CKD. DKK3 rose and UMOD fell with declining kidney function. – met all criteria for assessing mortality and nephrotoxicity, so these remain research-stage. - PMID:38280489

[C | emerging] Several reviews state that most novel CKD biomarkers still require validation in large, diverse populations before routine use. Current tests for identifying progressors perform poorly, and a biomarker panel is suggested as a reasonable future approach. - PMID:33375198, PMID:36041551, PMID:39298548

[C | evidence supported] Heart-failure biomarkers (BNP, NT-proBNP, troponin) are affected by renal insufficiency. Reviews suggest kidney-function-adjusted cut-offs and serial measurement, and note that natriuretic peptides and absolute troponin levels keep diagnostic and prognostic value in CKD and cardiorenal syndrome. - PMID:32710942, PMID:42652245

[C | evidence supported] A review states that kidney transplantation is an effective treatment for kidney failure in Alport syndrome. It reports outcomes comparable to, or better than, those in other causes of kidney failure. - PMID:39558650

[C | evidence supported] Post-transplant anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) nephritis after transplantation for Alport syndrome is described as rare but able to cause graft loss. The risk is noted especially in males with X-linked Alport syndrome, and de novo anti-GBM disease after transplant for Alport syndrome is a recognised phenomenon. - PMID:28515156, PMID:39558650

[C | evidence supported] Joint COL4A3/4/5 genetic analysis is described by guideline as the key diagnostic test for persistent haematuria, proteinuria or kidney failure of unknown origin. Cascade screening of first-degree relatives identifies variant carriers, many of whom already have kidney involvement. - PMID:39673454, PMID:42529192

[C | evidence supported] An older Danish series reported a mean ESRD age of 35.8 years for collagenous-domain glycine substitutions in males, compared with 21.6 years for truncating variants. It concluded that genotype is of limited usefulness for predicting prognosis. - PMID:19728970

[C | evidence supported] In a large multi-ethnic UK cohort, creatinine-based eGFR had the greatest difference from measured GFR and the lowest accuracy in South Asians. It overestimated measured GFR in young adults (<25 years), people with low BMI and people with hypoalbuminaemia. LMR and EKFC equations agreed better with measured GFR in South Asians and young adults. - PMID:42676916

[C | evidence supported] A recent review reports that the 2024 KDIGO guideline recommends equations combining creatinine and cystatin C for CKD diagnosis and staging. The review also states that cystatin C helps where creatinine is less reliable, such as with altered muscle mass, and is most prognostically informative when creatinine- and cystatin C-based eGFR differ widely. - PMID:42424121
[C | emerging] In ADPKD, slopes from combined creatinine–cystatin C eGFR correlated more strongly with measured-GFR decline and were less variable than creatinine-only slopes. - PMID:42733501
[C | guideline supported] An older CKD guideline recommends a low-potassium diet when GFR is below 20 ml/min, or below 50 ml/min if potassium-raising drugs are taken. - PMID:19018744

[C | evidence supported] KDIGO 2024, as reported in a 2026 narrative review, advises individualized potassium management. Its emphasis is on limiting foods rich in bioavailable potassium, especially processed foods, rather than reflexively restricting fruits and vegetables. The review notes that hyperkalemia risk is modified by kidney function, bowel function, metabolic acidosis, medications and food processing. - PMID:42650632

[C | guideline supported] The older guideline lists drugs that impair renal potassium excretion as main causes of hyperkalemia in CKD. It recommends checking potassium two weeks after starting an ACEi or ARB, and advises against routine aldosterone antagonists in advanced CKD. - PMID:19018744

[C | evidence supported] Older potassium binders (sodium and calcium polystyrene sulphonate), dietary restriction, bicarbonate, diuretics and RAASi down-titration are judged to have limited efficacy and poor tolerability for long-term potassium control. Newer binders such as sodium zirconium cyclosilicate are described as enabling rapid and sustained potassium control. - PMID:31800075, PMID:41953780

[C | emerging] A KDIGO 2024-based quality-improvement protocol in non-dialysis CKD defines hyperkalemia as serum potassium above 5.0 mmol/L and normokalemia as 3.5-5.0 mmol/L. It monitors potassium every 3 months, or monthly for high-risk patients. - PMID:42015032

[C | evidence supported] In a cross-sectional cohort of 5,046 adults with non-dialysis CKD and measured GFR, lower venous bicarbonate was independently associated with hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia was defined as plasma potassium ≥5.0 mmol/L or potassium binder use. Prevalence rose to 21% in CKD stages 4-5. This is an association, not proof that acidosis causes hyperkalemia. - PMID:42664185

[C | evidence supported] A 2026 narrative review states that hyperkalemia risk in CKD is modified by several factors: kidney function, bowel function, metabolic acidosis, diabetes, medications and food processing. It recommends correcting acidosis and constipation, reviewing potassium-raising medications, and monitoring potassium according to baseline risk, rather than reflexively restricting plant foods. - PMID:42650632

[C | evidence supported] CKD reviews state that patients require monitoring for complications that include both hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis. One review notes that guidelines recommend a target serum bicarbonate of at least 22 mmol/L, and that acidosis frequently goes undiagnosed. It also states that metabolic acidosis in CKD is associated with CKD progression, hyperkalemia and mortality. Together these support measuring bicarbonate alongside potassium. - PMID:31573641, PMID:36916426

[C | emerging] The potassium binder sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) increased serum bicarbonate in clinical trials designed around serum potassium. The proposed mechanism is gut binding of ammonium. This shows that potassium-lowering therapy and acid-base status interact. It is presented for physician awareness only, not as a treatment recommendation. - PMID:36916426

[C | emerging] In an observational study of non-dialysis CKD, higher record of certain vegetables was associated with lower odds of metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate <22 mmol/L). Reviews suggest that plant anions may mitigate acidosis. Plant-food restriction for hyperkalemia should be individualized rather than universal. - PMID:32528189, PMID:42380787

[C | evidence supported] RAAS blockade is described as the foundation of Alport syndrome treatment to delay kidney failure. A systematic review reports potential benefit of ramipril and losartan, but heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis. - PMID:40165927, PMID:41243004

[C | emerging] In kidney transplant recipients, hyperkalemia was associated with lower eGFR, not with SGLT2i treatment. RAAS inhibitor persistence did not differ between SGLT2i users and controls. - PMID:42682832

[C | evidence supported] Insufficient EPO production, from renal interstitial fibrosis or impaired oxygen sensing, is described as the fundamental mechanism initiating renal anemia. Inflammation, iron deficiency and CKD mineral-bone disorder are described as acting together to cause EPO resistance. - PMID:42610550, PMID:42923141

[C | evidence supported] Inflammation causes iron-restricted erythropoiesis through hepcidin-mediated retention of iron in the reticulo-endothelial system. Reviews list MCV, iron studies, percentage of hypochromic red cells, reticulocyte hemoglobin content, ferritin, sTfR, hepcidin, EPO and GDF15 as markers for characterizing this. - PMID:42496447, PMID:42656828

[C | evidence supported] Inflammation and infection can distort standard iron-deficiency tests. sTfR and the sTfR/log-ferritin index can complement ferritin in separating iron deficiency from anemia of inflammation, but sTfR is itself influenced by inflammation. SGLT2 inhibitors alter how ferritin should be interpreted. - PMID:23911105, PMID:33839163, PMID:42559859

[C | evidence supported] A Spanish position statement summarizes KDIGO 2026 as follows. Hb targets remain <11.5 g/dL. ESA initiation is individualized between 8.5 and 10 g/dL depending on cardiovascular risk, symptoms and transfusion needs. Dialysis thresholds are stated as ≥9-10 g/dL. - PMID:42414122

[C | evidence supported] The only interval-related statement in the sources concerns treatment dosing, not lab monitoring. KDIGO 2026, as summarized in the Spanish position statement, stresses using the lowest effective ESA or HIF-PHI dose, with adjustments every 4 weeks. - PMID:42414122

[C | evidence supported] The Spanish adaptation of KDIGO 2026 recommends withholding iron during systemic infections. It also notes that uncertainty persists about upper limits for ferritin and transferrin saturation. - PMID:42414122

[C | evidence supported] ESA therapy has been associated with cardiovascular events, particularly in hyporesponders requiring high doses or at high Hb targets. This supports the upper Hb ceiling. - PMID:42795843

[C | evidence supported] A meta-analysis of 36 RCTs found that HIF-PHIs did not significantly increase MACE or mortality. It did report a hyperkalemia signal in non-dialysis-dependent patients. KDIGO nonetheless prefers ESAs first line. (verified with caveat) - PMID:42819330

[C | emerging] The composite RDW-to-albumin ratio (RAR) was independently associated with all-cause mortality in three settings: peritoneal dialysis patients, dialysis patients with coronary artery disease, and a NHANES-based CKD cohort. - PMID:41742052, PMID:42110186, PMID:42789467

[C | hypothesis] Reviews state that it has not been established whether elevated RDW is causal or an epiphenomenon. Elevated RDW reflects disordered erythropoiesis and red cell survival linked to inflammation, oxidative stress, poor nutrition and altered erythropoietin function. In CKD anemia, iron deficiency is described as the most important factor in erythropoietin hyporesponsiveness. - PMID:16551293, PMID:25535770

[C | emerging] Post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis or disease is reported in about 5% (up to 5%) of patients with Alport syndrome. This figure is not broken down by sex or inheritance mode in the sources. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934

[C | evidence supported] COL4A5 defects account for most cases of post-transplant anti-GBM disease. The alloantibody target in X-linked disease is mainly the alpha5(IV) NC1 domain; in autosomal recessive disease it is alpha3(IV). - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] Anti-GBM nephritis usually causes graft failure within weeks to months of the first transplant and rarely beyond the first year. Once nephritis develops, progression to graft loss is often rapid. A subset of patients produce anti-GBM antibodies without ever developing clinical nephritis. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934

[C | evidence supported] The clinical course and prognosis in Alport spectrum disorder are highly variable. They are influenced by sex, mode of inheritance, affected gene, mutation type and genetic modifiers. - PMID:39004457

[C | emerging] In a WES cohort, 13.1% of living kidney donors carried variants associated with latent renal or systemic conditions despite no clinical manifestation at donation. This supports the potential value of genomic screening of donors. - PMID:41194031

[C | evidence supported] Genetic diagnosis with joint analysis of COL4A3/4/5 is the key diagnostic test. Routine exon-based analysis misses a pathogenic variant in 10-20% of XLAS patients, and mRNA analysis can confirm pathogenicity of splice-region VUS. - PMID:39673454, PMID:42254845

[C | evidence supported] Expert consensus treats position-1 Gly residues of Gly-X-Y repeats in the intermediate collagenous domain as mutational hotspots (PM1). The same consensus notes that hypomorphic variants are often Gly residues adjacent to a non-collagenous interruption, which complicates benign-frequency thresholds. - PMID:33854215

[C | evidence supported] A 2026 narrative review reports that the 2024 KDIGO guideline recommends equations combining serum creatinine and cystatin C for CKD diagnosis and staging. It also reports that cystatin C-inclusive equations generally outperform creatinine-based equations in bias and accuracy. No GFR-stratified data, including for G5, are given. - PMID:42424121

[C | evidence supported] In 644 patients with iohexol-measured GFR (mean 50.4, range 12-150 mL/min/1.73m2), a combined creatinine-cystatin C formula reached the highest P30 (87.0%) and the best CKD stage classification (70.2-73.9%). Two cystatin C assays diverged by about 40% in the low GFR range, so equation-assay matching becomes critical at low GFR. - PMID:17911090

[C | emerging] In 260 ADPKD patients, batch-measured combined creatinine-cystatin C eGFR slopes correlated more strongly with iothalamate-measured GFR decline than creatinine-only slopes. Combined estimates were described as enhancing precision and reducing slope variability. Cystatin-containing equations showed greater cross-sectional bias than creatinine-only eGFR. - PMID:42733501

[C | evidence supported] In pooled CKD-EPI development data (13,391 individuals, 26 studies), deviation between eGFR and mGFR was attributed to three sources: study variation (about 10-40%), mGFR measurement error (20-40%) and patient-level eGFR error (20-70%). Individual estimates therefore carry substantial uncertainty even when population-average performance is acceptable. - PMID:42804441

[C | emerging] A review of acute-on-chronic kidney disease reports that creatinine-based definitions show reduced prognostic accuracy in CKD populations. It reports that cystatin C-based eGFR shows superior discrimination for mortality and progression. - PMID:42954720
[C | evidence supported] Non-renal influences on cystatin C, notably steroid therapy and possibly malignancy, remain a concern for its use as a GFR marker. - PMID:11928770

[C | emerging] In a large ethnically diverse UK cohort, creatinine-based eGFR had the greatest difference and lowest accuracy in South Asians, and LMR and EKFC showed improved agreement with measured GFR, particularly in South Asians and young adults. Results are not reported by CKD stage in the abstract. - PMID:42676916

[C | emerging] In this cohort, measured GFR was substantially overestimated by creatinine equations in young adults (<25 years), in people with low BMI (<20 kg/m2) and in hypoalbuminaemia (<20 g/L). - PMID:42676916

[C | evidence supported] A systematic review and meta-analysis in South Asians found creatinine-based equations overestimate mGFR, with all creatinine and cystatin C equations below the 75% P30 accuracy threshold. Combined creatinine-cystatin C equations had the best accuracy (P30 79-82%). EKFC was not quantitatively evaluated and was flagged as needing population-specific calibration. - PMID:41550526
[C | emerging] In young adults aged 18-25, EKFC and r-LMR had better bias and P30 than CKD-EPI. The possible exception was hyperfiltration (GFR ≥120). - PMID:39314869
[C | emerging] Compared with CKD-EPI 2021, EKFC staged CKD differently in patients with eGFR below 60, but produced a similar number of end-stage renal failure cases. - PMID:37534520

[C | emerging] A cystatin C-based EKFC equation was unbiased in European, US and African cohorts, and averaging EKFC creatinine and cystatin C estimates further improved accuracy. South Asian cohorts were not included. - PMID:36720134

[C | evidence supported] As reported by a narrative review, KDIGO 2024 advises individualized potassium management that emphasizes limiting foods rich in bioavailable potassium, particularly processed foods, rather than reflexively restricting fruits and vegetables. This is secondary reporting, not primary guideline text. - PMID:42650632

[C | evidence supported] Across CKD studies, the association between dietary and serum potassium is reported as weak or inconsistent. Hyperkalemia risk is modified by kidney function, bowel function, metabolic acidosis, diabetes, medications, food processing and food matrix. The review proposes monitoring serum potassium according to baseline risk and reviewing potassium-raising medications and additives. - PMID:42650632

[C | emerging] A KDIGO-2024-based quality-improvement trial protocol operationally defines hyperkalemia as serum potassium >5.0 mmol/L and normokalemia as 3.5-5.0 mmol/L. It monitors potassium every 3 months, or monthly in high-risk patients. These are protocol definitions; the sources do not confirm them as KDIGO 2024 recommendations. - PMID:42015032

[C | evidence supported] Secondary sources report that KDIGO 2024 notes the use of newer potassium binders to manage hyperkalemia and enable optimal use of guideline-directed medical therapy, such as RAS inhibitors. - PMID:40434618

[C | evidence supported] Narrative reviews report patiromer as well tolerated and effective for lowering serum potassium in CKD over up to one year of use, with short-term follow-up showing minimal adverse events for both patiromer and SZC. - PMID:28212180

[C | evidence supported] SZC is described as selectively binding potassium in the gut, with about 1 year of safety data for chronic use and rapid onset. No head-to-head comparisons among available binders exist. - PMID:34227913

[C | emerging] In a small randomized crossover trial in advanced CKD on RAAS inhibitors, a potassium-rich diet gave noninferior serum potassium at 6 weeks. The few hyperkalemia episodes (5.9 and 6.1 mmol/L) were managed with SZC, after which the diet continued without recurrence. - PMID:42636918

[C | evidence supported] Most of the evidence framing for novel binders in CKD centres on enabling continued or optimized RAASi therapy, rather than on binder benefit independent of RAASi. - PMID:40434618, PMID:41953780

[C | hypothesis] In a large propensity-matched observational study of heart failure with hyperkalaemia, SZC was associated with higher mortality and HF hospitalization than sodium polystyrene sulfonate, and with higher HF hospitalization than patiromer. Patiromer was associated with lower HF hospitalization but slightly higher mortality than sodium polystyrene sulfonate. The authors consider these findings hypothesis-generating. - PMID:42802363

[C | emerging] In an open-label RCT in type 2 diabetes with hyperkalemia, SZC failed to demonstrate noninferiority to a potassium-restricted diet for normokalemia, though mean potassium was lower. One sudden death occurred in the SZC group. - PMID:42423524

[C | evidence supported] Metabolic acidosis is recognised as a cause of hyperkalaemia through a transcellular shift of potassium out of cells. This is distinct from the impaired renal potassium excretion seen in CKD. The source states the category of mechanism but not its cellular basis. - PMID:42629001

[C | evidence supported] In CKD, the hyperkalaemia risk linked to potassium record is modified by metabolic acidosis, alongside kidney function, bowel function, diabetes/hyperglycaemia and medications. Correcting acidosis is listed as part of individualised potassium management. - PMID:35942480, PMID:42650632

[C | evidence supported] In acute hyperkalaemia, sodium bicarbonate is described as an adjunct limited to patients with concurrent metabolic acidosis rather than a routine potassium-lowering therapy. Its role is described as uncertain. - PMID:41506858, PMID:42935704

[D | emerging] Pre-analytical factors can falsely elevate measured serum potassium even without hemolysis. Prolonged refrigerated storage of blood samples before analysis increased potassium by on average 5% at 4 h and 20% at 8 h. A repeat sample in the index case was 1.3 mmol/L lower. - PMID:42651077

[D | hypothesis] In a cohort of 305 children with chronic renal failure (GFR <50 mL/min/1.73 m2), anemia was marked at presentation (mean Hb 7.6 g/dL), alongside late referral and malnutrition. This is descriptive context that anemia accompanies advanced CKD; it does not explain mechanism or causation. - PMID:14660834

[D | hypothesis] In 18 adults with genetically confirmed Alport syndrome given RASi plus SGLT2i, hemoglobin increase was reported as a secondary effect. This association does not apply directly to a patient at eGFR 6.2 with no recorded medications. - PMID:42006198

[D | hypothesis] In critically ill non-trauma emergency department patients, anemia (Hb <12 g/dL) on admission was independently associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 2.07). This is a setting-specific prognostic association, not evidence about outpatient CKD anemia. - PMID:42907747

[D | hypothesis] Acute events such as surgery and anaesthetic technique can change RDW over 24 hours, so timing relative to procedures is a confounder. The CV vs SD reporting format also matters. - PMID:42937722

[D | hypothesis] Related composite indices combining RDW with other routine tests have been studied as prognostic markers: RDW-albumin ratio, haemoglobin-to-RDW ratio and RDW-to-platelet ratio. CRP and NLR are reported alongside RDW. All have only modest discrimination or limited data. - PMID:41246322, PMID:42665987

[D | emerging] Several urinary and inflammatory biomarkers remain research-only. These include urinary podocin, VEGF-A, EGF, TGF-β1, HMGB1, MCP-1 and miRNA-21. A pediatric narrative review states no podocyte-derived urinary marker has yet been shown to add information beyond proteinuria and filtration rate. - PMID:35806283, PMID:42942308
[D | emerging] Sensorineural hearing loss is described as a frequent early extra-renal sign of Alport syndrome that is relevant to renal prognosis. - PMID:16878253

[D | hypothesis] Glomerular spatial transcriptomics and canine X-linked nephropathy urinary tubular markers (RBP, β2-microglobulin, NAG, NGAL, IgG) are hypothesis-generating only. - PMID:22356524, PMID:38516889

[D | hypothesis] Among pathogenic COL4A5 glycine substitutions in males, substitution with a highly destabilising residue reduced median age at kidney failure by 7 years and age at hearing-loss diagnosis by 21 years. The same study lists the highly destabilising residues as Arg, Val, Glu, Asp and Trp. Substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region delayed kidney failure by 19 years, and exon location had no effect. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 glycine substitutions adjacent to non-collagenous regions are over-represented in the normal population (gnomAD). Proximity to an interruption is therefore relevant to how much weight a glycine VUS can be given toward pathogenicity. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] Several non-sequencing approaches could add pathogenicity evidence. In a cell assay, trimer secretion was reduced for all glycine mutants with early renal failure, and the authors suggest it may help separate pathogenic from nonpathogenic variants. Absence of alpha5(IV) on skin-biopsy immunostaining supports X-linked Alport syndrome. Cascade testing found additional affected relatives in all tested families. - PMID:19728970, PMID:32405592, PMID:42552945

[D | guideline supported] For hyperkalemia without symptoms or ECG abnormalities, the older guideline considers medication review, dietary potassium restriction and oral ion-exchange resins usually sufficient. With symptoms and/or ECG abnormalities it recommends the usual parenteral measures (strength A). (verified with caveat) - PMID:19018744

[D | guideline supported] Metabolic acidosis, constipation and prolonged fasting are listed as contributors to hyperkalemia in CKD. Moderate metabolic acidosis is common below GFR 20 ml/min. (verified with caveat) - PMID:19018744

[D | guideline supported] The older guideline advises considering hemodialysis at GFR below 10 ml/min in the hyperkalemia context. A 2019 review similarly notes that hyperkalemia is an indication to begin renal replacement therapy in end-stage renal disease. (verified with caveat) - PMID:19018744, PMID:31800075

[D | hypothesis] A case report describes severe metabolic acidosis with hypokalemia in a patient with stage 3 CKD. It was attributed to topical brinzolamide (a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor eye drop). This shows that acidosis in CKD does not uniformly raise potassium, and that hidden medications can drive acid-base disorders. - PMID:42410525

[D | emerging] In a small case series, adding spironolactone to ACEi or ACEi+ARB in Alport patients with good renal function reduced proteinuria. Serum potassium rose slightly, without severe hyperkalemia (>5.0 mEq/l). - PMID:17039334

[D | hypothesis] In COL4A3-/- mice, adding spironolactone to ramipril reduced proteinuria and fibrosis but did not extend survival beyond ACEi monotherapy. The authors attribute this possibly to adverse effects such as hyperkalemia and call for close monitoring. - PMID:34209341

[D | hypothesis] A review describes finerenone as having a reduced risk of hyperkalemia compared with steroidal MRAs. Evidence comes mainly from diabetic populations, not Alport syndrome. - PMID:41501973
[D | hypothesis] In a small retrospective case-control study of maintenance hemodialysis patients, higher RDW was independently associated with late arteriovenous fistula thrombosis. - PMID:41909600

[D | hypothesis] Variant type is the only genotype risk factor stated in the sources. COL4A5 gene deletions are more commonly associated with post-transplant anti-GBM disease than point mutations. No source specifically assesses glycine missense variants for this complication. - PMID:14717941

[D | hypothesis] After a first graft is lost to anti-GBM nephritis, recurrence with accelerated graft loss on retransplantation is reported. Anti-T-cell therapy, plasma exchange and mycophenolate did not prevent graft loss in reported cases. There is no agreed protocol for treatment or prophylaxis. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934
[D | hypothesis] Standard anti-GBM ELISA may fail to detect Alport alloantibodies. Western blotting against the alpha5(IV) NC1 domain was more sensitive and specific in a case series. - PMID:14717941

[D | hypothesis] A recent case series of three genetically confirmed transplanted Alport patients (two X-linked) reports generally favourable outcomes. One X-linked recipient developed late antibody-mediated rejection at six years. The abstract does not report anti-GBM nephritis in these cases. - PMID:42076904

[D | emerging] In a single-centre case series of four males with severe MYH9-related Epstein syndrome (a different hereditary nephritis), early and accurate diagnosis enabled pre-emptive living-donor transplantation in two patients. No comparative outcomes versus post-dialysis transplantation were reported. - PMID:29532554

[D | emerging] A small Indian retrospective series reports that ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation using immunoadsorption desensitization (with structured column reuse) was feasible, with 100% patient and graft survival at three months. - PMID:41552072

[D | emerging] Female COL4A5 heterozygotes are not merely asymptomatic carriers and may progress to kidney failure. This is illustrated in a pedigree where the heterozygous maternal grandmother reached end-stage disease. - PMID:42255916

[D | emerging] X-linked Alport syndrome has a variable presentation in females. A heterozygous woman with COL4A5 p.Gly1196Glu had chronic proteinuria that transiently reached nephrotic range postpartum. - PMID:41799611
[D | emerging] Kidney transplantation in Alport syndrome is described as effective when guided by molecular confirmation and careful donor evaluation. - PMID:42076904

[D | hypothesis] In a database genotype-phenotype analysis, COL4A5 Gly substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region (interruption or terminus) were associated with delayed kidney failure. COL4A5 variants adjacent to non-collagenous regions were also over-represented in gnomAD. Whether Gly1048 meets this adjacency definition is not stated in any source. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 Gly substitutions to a highly destabilising residue were associated with earlier kidney failure in males. Glu is explicitly listed as highly destabilising in the same study's COL4A3/COL4A4 analysis; the patient's variant is Gly1048Glu. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] The α5(IV) triple-helical domain is interrupted 22 times by non-collagenous sequences. Older case reports localise specific glycines between numbered interruptions (Gly852 between 16 and 17; Gly1143 between 19 and 20), but none localises Gly1048. - PMID:1376965, PMID:7969679, PMID:8893151
[D | hypothesis] Even with an identical COL4A5 Gly substitution, the age at onset of renal failure and the presence of extrarenal features varied among relatives. - PMID:7969679

[D | hypothesis] In elderly Chinese inpatients, no creatinine-based equation, including EKFC and LMR, performed well. Accuracy was particularly poor at mGFR below 30, illustrating that creatinine equations may be less reliable at low GFR. - PMID:37542000

[D | hypothesis] Clinicians in a national CKD clinic network ranked hyperkalemia-prevention strategies and the effects of dietary restriction as research priorities arising from the KDIGO 2024 guideline. This suggests these areas remain incompletely evidenced. - PMID:42472272

[D | hypothesis] Cost-effectiveness microsimulation models included advanced CKD (stages 3a-5) and found SZC cost-effective or cost-saving. However, SZC was most cost-effective in less severe CKD with concurrent RAASi use. - PMID:38318718, PMID:38443742

[D | hypothesis] One review lists 'mineral metabolic acidosis' as a cause of transcellular potassium shift, separately from diabetic ketoacidosis. It does not explain or quantify any difference between mineral and organic acidosis. The diabetic ketoacidosis example is confounded by insulin deficiency, which a human review lists as its own shift mechanism. The source is veterinary. - PMID:41929733

[E | hypothesis] The provided sources contain no report of COL4A5 p.Gly1048Glu (c.3143G>A). Its pathogenicity cannot be established from this evidence set. The general variant class is the most frequent pathogenic class in Alport syndrome: glycine substitutions in the Gly-Xaa-Yaa collagenous domain. - PMID:19728970, PMID:35177655

[E | hypothesis] In the phase 2 lademirsen RCT in adults with Alport syndrome (eGFR >35 to <90), anemia was among the treatment-emergent adverse events reported in both treatment and placebo groups. The abstract does not characterise its type, mechanism or frequency relative to other CKD causes, so it does not show that Alport-associated anemia is distinct. - PMID:38829703

blocks.text: Verified research findings (62)

items: [A | guideline supported] KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD guidance for adults with CKD G3a-G5 advises basing treatment on trends in laboratory values rather than a single abnormal result. It also advises caution to avoid hypercalcemia when treating secondary hyperparathyroidism. This applies to mineral-bone parameters, not to eGFR targets. - PMID:29459980

[A | guideline supported] The KDIGO 2026 graded recommendations set an upper Hb target below 11.5 g/dL (<115 g/L) during ESA maintenance therapy. The Hb threshold for starting an ESA is individualised to patient characteristics, symptoms and values, rather than being a single fixed number. - PMID:42735412

[A | guideline supported] KDIGO 2026 recommends addressing correctable causes of anaemia before using an ESA or a HIF-PHI. It recommends using TSAT and ferritin thresholds to guide iron therapy, and an ESA rather than a HIF-PHI as first-line treatment. Intravenous iron is preferred over oral iron in people receiving haemodialysis. - PMID:42414122, PMID:42735412

[A | guideline supported] An international guideline (ERKNet/ERA/ESPN 2024, based on systematic literature review and graded consensus) recommends that relatives with heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants be considered only as a last-resort living kidney donor source. The abstract does not report the post-donation outcome data underlying this recommendation. - PMID:39673454

[B | guideline supported] The 2024 ERKNet/ERA/ESPN Alport guideline states that relatives with heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants should be considered only as the last possible resource for living kidney donation. - PMID:39673454

[B | guideline supported] The ERKNet/ERA/ESPN guideline identifies joint COL4A3/4/5 genetic analysis as the key diagnostic test in persons presenting with kidney failure of unknown origin, persistent haematuria or proteinuria. It does not specify kidney-function monitoring intervals for X-linked males with kidney failure in the abstract. - PMID:39673454

[B | evidence supported] In non-diabetic advanced CKD, targeting a higher Hb (11-13 g/dL) with darbepoetin alfa did not improve the kidney composite outcome compared with a lower target (9-11 g/dL). Achieved mean Hb was 11.2 vs 10.0 g/dL. - PMID:32245781

[B | evidence supported] In the same trial, cardiovascular events did not differ significantly between the higher and lower Hb target groups. The authors note, however, that earlier large Western RCTs targeting higher Hb with ESAs showed harm, and that effects may differ between CKD subpopulations. - PMID:32245781

[B | guideline supported] The 2024 international Alport guideline recommends that relatives carrying heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants be considered only as the last possible resource for living kidney donation. In X-linked disease, this is relevant to maternal-line female relatives, who may be heterozygous COL4A5 carriers. - PMID:39673454

[C | guideline supported] ASN guidance identifies longitudinal (serial) assessment of eGFR and albuminuria as foundational markers of cardiovascular and kidney risk. The abstract does not specify a target eGFR value or a reassessment interval for CKD G5. - PMID:42684397

[C | guideline supported] ASN guidance suggests that integrating risk prediction models, including the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE), may support early identification of high-risk patients and guide treatment intensification. - PMID:42684397

[C | guideline supported] The ASN guidance explicitly acknowledges important evidence gaps for advanced CKD, dialysis, transplant recipients, younger individuals and nonmetabolic (glomerular) kidney diseases. All of these categories are relevant to a 23-year-old with X-linked Alport syndrome and CKD G5. - PMID:42684397

[C | evidence supported] Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault) and CKD-EPI eGFR are not interchangeable. Discordant drug-dose categories occur in 4-34% of patients, with the largest discrepancies in those with the lowest measured function. - PMID:42939623

[C | emerging] Observational target-trial emulation in haemodialysis patients on darbepoetin compared Hb targets. Targeting 105-125 g/L was not associated with increased mortality versus 95-115 g/L. Targeting above 125 g/L may increase mortality risk, but the estimate was imprecise. No reassessment interval was reported as a guideline objective. - PMID:42893801

[C | evidence supported] Care of adults with advanced CKD (stage 4-5, not on KRT) is described as including recommended laboratory assessments and interdisciplinary support for KRT planning (dialysis, transplantation or conservative management). The abstract does not specify monitoring frequencies or planning thresholds. - PMID:39124645

[C | evidence supported] Patients with advanced CKD and evidence of progression are at high risk of needing renal replacement therapy. Specialised transition clinics are proposed to prepare them, emphasising pre-emptive transplantation, planned dialysis start, access placement and shared decision-making. No timing thresholds are given in the abstract. - PMID:32162667

[C | guideline supported] ASN Kidney Health Guidance emphasises longitudinal assessment of eGFR and albuminuria as foundational risk markers and notes that the KFRE may support early identification of high-risk patients. It also highlights evidence gaps in advanced CKD, younger individuals and glomerular disorders. - PMID:42684397

[C | evidence supported] KDIGO 2024 guidelines advise individualised potassium management, and the review recommends monitoring serum potassium according to baseline risk. No specific frequency is given. - PMID:42650632

[C | evidence supported] A 2025 review summarising the updated ERKNet/ERA/ESPN criteria reports that carrier donation is generally avoided. It may be considered only in highly selected individuals over 40 years with preserved kidney function and no subclinical kidney damage on biopsy, with individualised evaluation of potential donors from affected families. - PMID:42147990

[C | evidence supported] Earlier expert guidelines (2022) recommend that COL4A3 or COL4A4 heterozygotes do not act as kidney donors and advocate cascade testing of first-degree relatives because of their risk of impaired kidney function. - PMID:34930753

[C | evidence supported] Variants of uncertain significance should not independently determine treatment or donor eligibility. Variants must be evaluated against gene-disease validity, inheritance, segregation, molecular mechanism and phenotype. Molecular diagnosis enables cascade testing and safer assessment of living-related donors. - PMID:42792963
[C | emerging] The 2024 International Workshop highlighted challenges in variant interpretation and misclassification, especially for non-European populations. - PMID:41853742

[C | evidence supported] The Spanish Society of Nephrology adaptation of KDIGO 2026 gives numbers for initiation. It describes Hb targets of <11.5 g/dL, with individualised initiation between 8.5 and 10 g/dL depending on cardiovascular risk, symptoms and transfusion needs. It describes the dialysis threshold as about 9-10 g/dL. It also stresses the lowest effective ESA or HIF-PHI dose, with adjustments every 4 weeks. - PMID:42414122
[C | evidence supported] Patient Blood Management strategies to reduce transfusions are emphasised, particularly in kidney transplant candidates. - PMID:42414122

[C | evidence supported] A CKD review summarising guidelines defines absolute iron deficiency as TSAT ≤20% with ferritin ≤100 ng/mL in predialysis and peritoneal dialysis patients, or ≤200 ng/mL in haemodialysis patients. Functional iron deficiency (iron-restricted erythropoiesis) is TSAT ≤20% with elevated ferritin. - PMID:30970355

[C | evidence supported] The same review states that iron supplementation is recommended for all CKD patients with anaemia. IV iron is preferred in dialysis (5D), and either IV or oral iron is recommended in non-dialysis CKD stages 3–5. - PMID:30970355

[C | evidence supported] An older CKD convention identified iron deficiency as ferritin <100 μg/L regardless of TSAT, or ferritin 100–299 μg/L if TSAT <20%. A heart-failure review argues this definition was set to boost ESA responsiveness rather than on evidence of tissue iron depletion. - PMID:38733252

[C | guideline supported] A systematic review of 29 iron-deficiency guidelines found that, in CKD, some guidelines cap ferritin during iron therapy at 500 μg/L (5 guidelines) or 800 μg/L (5 guidelines). Nine guidelines set TSAT targets, ranging from 20% to 50%. Overall, it suggests diagnostic cut-offs of ferritin 100 μg/L and TSAT 20% in most conditions. - PMID:26561626

[C | guideline supported] Taiwan practice guidelines used a broader CKD iron-deficiency criterion of ferritin <300 ng/mL and/or TSAT <30%. They paired early IV iron with low-dose ESA aiming at Hb 10–11 g/dL. - PMID:25156587

[C | evidence supported] The 2026 KDIGO anaemia guideline, as described in the ERBP commentary, introduces more proactive IV iron thresholds, especially for haemodialysis. It keeps ESAs as preferred first-line therapy and stresses evaluation for causes of anaemia other than erythropoietin deficiency. The specific thresholds are not given in the abstract. - PMID:41604211

[C | evidence supported] Outside inflammatory conditions, iron deficiency is diagnosed by ferritin typically <30 ng/mL or TSAT <20%. IV iron is indicated in chronic inflammatory conditions including CKD. - PMID:40159291

[C | emerging] Ferritin can be raised independently of iron stores by kidney failure, infection and inflammation, and may be distorted by SGLT2 inhibitors. Percentage of hypochromic red cells (%HYPO) and reticulocyte haemoglobin content (CHr) are described as the most specific markers of iron-deficient erythropoiesis in non-dialysis CKD. - PMID:28963827, PMID:35699322, PMID:38733252

[C | emerging] A CKD review highlights a potential risk from newer IV iron agents of hypophosphataemia and 6H syndrome, which includes hypocalcaemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism. This is relevant to safety monitoring if IV iron is considered. - PMID:34758368

[C | evidence supported] The ERBP commentary on the KDIGO 2026 CKD anaemia guideline emphasises comprehensive evaluation for causes of anaemia other than erythropoietin insufficiency, individualised timing and type of treatment, and ESAs as preferred first-line therapy over HIF-PHIs. The abstract does not state a numeric Hb target. It notes that some special aspects are not covered by KDIGO, including pregnancy, gender-specific considerations, and SGLT2-inhibitor and inflammation interactions. - PMID:41604211

[C | emerging] In non-dialysis CKD patients with Hb below 10 g/dL who were ESA-naive, darbepoetin alfa treated to a 10-12 g/dL target corrected anaemia in nearly all subjects, with similar safety for monthly versus every-2-week dosing. This shows the target range used in trials, not evidence that it is the optimal target. - PMID:24506498

[C | guideline supported] The KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline synopsis highlights greater emphasis on cystatin C for GFR assessment and a shift to an individualized, risk-based approach to predicting kidney failure. The abstract does not specify monitoring intervals for G5 or KRT/dialysis timing. - PMID:40063957

[C | guideline supported] The KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline is not intended for people receiving dialysis or with a kidney transplant. Its scope includes evaluation, risk assessment and management to delay progression and complications in CKD. - PMID:38519239

[C | evidence supported] A primary-care review emphasizes risk-based nephrology referral integrating eGFR decline, albuminuria severity and kidney failure risk equations, together with shared decision-making about renal replacement therapy. - PMID:41152063

[C | evidence supported] Guidelines across societies agree on systematic assessment of eGFR and albuminuria, with confirmation of abnormalities and regular monitoring. The abstract does not specify a frequency. - PMID:42422469

[C | emerging] A review of acute-on-chronic kidney disease reports that creatinine-based definitions have reduced prognostic accuracy in CKD, while cystatin C-based eGFR shows superior discrimination for mortality and progression. Acute deterioration superimposed on CKD is described as carrying increased mortality. - PMID:42954720

[C | emerging] In a UK advanced-CKD cohort, the 4- and 8-variable KFREs were compared against eGFR cut-offs of <20 and <15 mL/min/1.73m2 for guiding further treatment. On decision curve analysis, the KFRE gave better net clinical benefit than these eGFR-based thresholds. The cut-offs were study comparators, not guideline-endorsed transplant referral or waitlisting criteria. - PMID:34030639

[C | emerging] The KFRE's endpoint, ESRD, was defined as dialysis or pre-emptive transplantation within 2 and 5 years. Discrimination for this endpoint was good: AUC about 0.80 at 2 years for the 4-variable equation. - PMID:34030639

[C | evidence supported] A 2022 expert guideline recommends that COL4A3 or COL4A4 heterozygotes not act as kidney donors. It also advocates cascade testing of first-degree relatives because they are at risk of impaired kidney function. - PMID:34930753

[C | guideline supported] Genetic diagnosis using joint COL4A3/4/5 analysis is considered the key diagnostic test. Transplantation outcomes in Alport syndrome are described as favourable when guided by molecular confirmation and careful donor evaluation. - PMID:39673454, PMID:42076904
[C | evidence supported] De novo anti-GBM disease after kidney transplantation for Alport syndrome is a recognised but reportedly uncommon complication. - PMID:28515156, PMID:36252931

[C | emerging] In a prospective whole-exome sequencing cohort, 13.1% of clinically unaffected kidney donors carried variants associated with latent renal or systemic conditions. This supports genomic screening as part of donor evaluation. - PMID:41194031

[C | evidence supported] De novo anti-GBM nephritis is a recognised Alport-specific complication after kidney transplantation. Reported frequency ranges from about 3-5% of Alport recipients (reviews) to 1.4% of Alport recipients and 2% of males with COL4A5 mutations in a genotyped cohort. - PMID:28515156, PMID:29854973, PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] Post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis clusters in Alport patients with 'severe' mutations. In older molecular data, a COL4A5 deletion patient and a splice-site patient developed anti-GBM antibodies after transplantation. However, two other post-transplant anti-GBM cases had no COL4A5 lesion found. The abstracts do not classify glycine-substitution missense variants as severe or non-severe. - PMID:1450636, PMID:29854973

[C | evidence supported] Mutation severity did not significantly affect overall patient or graft survival after transplantation in Alport syndrome. Overall patient and graft survival in Alport recipients did not differ from matched non-Alport recipients. - PMID:1468159, PMID:29854973

[C | evidence supported] Mechanism: in X-linked Alport syndrome, the donor glomerular basement membrane presents a non-tolerised α3α4α5(IV) antigen. The alloantigen most often implicated in X-linked recipients with post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis is α5(IV). This form is immunologically distinct from classic Goodpasture disease. - PMID:42390934

[C | evidence supported] Timing and course: anti-GBM-related allograft failure typically occurs within weeks to months and usually not beyond the first year, and progression to graft loss is often rapid. Recurrence with accelerated rejection is reported after retransplantation in patients who lost a first graft to anti-GBM nephritis. - PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] Anti-GBM antibodies can appear after transplantation without clinical nephritis (isolated immunological anti-GBM disease). In one 30-patient series, antibodies were only transiently detected in one patient, with linear IgG staining but no nephritis. - PMID:1468159, PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] There is no agreed protocol for prophylaxis or treatment of post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis in Alport syndrome. Reported strategies vary (steroids combined with tacrolimus, azathioprine or ciclosporin), and plasmapheresis can be used to remove pathogenic antibodies. - PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] Reviews recommend that molecular confirmation and genetic evaluation of related living donor candidates inform transplant planning in monogenic kidney disease. Graft outcomes from donors with thin basement membrane disease were equivalent to those from donors with isolated hematuria and normal histology, but that cohort was not genetically stratified. - PMID:38481491, PMID:42076904, PMID:42922936

[C | evidence supported] A narrative review states that variants of uncertain significance should not independently determine treatment or donor eligibility. It also notes that molecular diagnosis can support safer assessment of living-related donors. - PMID:42792963

[C | emerging] In an observational cohort of 270 transplant candidates, standardized genetic testing guided living donor risk assessment and was reported to support safe living donor selection. Donor long-term kidney outcomes were not reported. - PMID:42017070

[D | emerging] Kidney transplantation is described as the best treatment modality for end-stage kidney disease and as effective in Alport syndrome when guided by molecular confirmation and careful donor evaluation. In a small case series, vascular events and late antibody-mediated rejection affected graft courses, supporting individualised post-transplant surveillance. - PMID:42076904, PMID:42147990

[D | emerging] Case reports describe good long-term graft outcomes after transplantation in genetically confirmed Alport syndrome, including X-linked disease. They also report rejection, vascular events, and immunosuppression-related complications. - PMID:42076904, PMID:42877346

[D | emerging] In a COL4A5 family, the mother of two affected brothers was herself on haemodialysis. This illustrates that mothers in the maternal line can have kidney failure themselves, consistent with this patient's family history. - PMID:42877346

[D | hypothesis] Beyond anti-GBM disease, a small genotype-guided case series in X-linked Alport recipients reported a COVID-19-associated graft arterial thrombosis requiring nephrectomy and late antibody-mediated rejection at 6 years. The authors concluded that individualized surveillance is needed. - PMID:42076904

[D | hypothesis] Female COL4A5 heterozygotes can have clinically significant kidney disease. One case report describes a heterozygous girl with persistent haematuria and proteinuria due to a COL4A5 variant. The same source states that genetic confirmation is essential for donor selection. - PMID:41483114

[D | hypothesis] A small case series (three transplanted Alport patients) concluded that transplantation is effective when guided by molecular confirmation and careful donor evaluation. It does not report outcomes in heterozygous donors. - PMID:42076904

Verified research findings (56)

items: [A | established] Clinical practice guidelines describe early renin-angiotensin system blockade as standard-of-care therapy in COL4A3/4/5 (Alport) glomerulopathy. This is a statement of direction only; no quantitative delay to kidney failure is given in the abstracts. - PMID:39673454, PMID:42316418

[A | established] An international guideline states that early renin-angiotensin system blockade is the standard of care in COL4A3/4/5 glomerulopathy. SGLT2 inhibitors may be added in adults with proteinuria and CKD. - PMID:39673454

[A | guideline supported] A 2026 Korean guideline, based on a GRADE systematic review, strongly recommends early RAS blockade as the cornerstone of Alport syndrome management. It reports the greatest benefit when blockade starts at the microscopic hematuria or microalbuminuria stage, the stage EARLY PRO-TECT enrolled. - PMID:42316418

[B | evidence supported] In meta-analyses of RCTs in adults with CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors versus placebo improved eGFR slope. In CKD with eGFR <60, the mean difference was 1.17 mL/min/1.73m2/yr for total slope and 2.12 for chronic slope. ESKD risk was reduced by about 30% (RR 0.70). - PMID:39487413, PMID:42741446

[B | evidence supported] In advanced CKD (eGFR 15–30), SGLT2 inhibitors slowed annual eGFR decline by 1.24 mL/min/1.73m2/yr and reduced the composite kidney outcome by 23%. A separate meta-analysis found a CKD4 subgroup renal composite RR of 0.78. - PMID:36316605, PMID:39487413
[B | evidence supported] An individual-participant meta-analysis of 23,340 empagliflozin trial participants reported:
64% slowing of chronic annual eGFR decline.
34% reduction in kidney failure.
Benefits irrespective of primary cause of kidney disease, level of kidney function and albuminuria. - PMID:41082889
[B | evidence supported] Reported SGLT2i harms in CKD meta-analyses include:
Increased diabetic ketoacidosis (RR 2.06).
Increased volume depletion (RR 1.28–1.36).

blocks.text: In eGFR <60, lower hyperkalemia and AKI risk were reported. - PMID:39487413, PMID:42741446

items: [B | guideline supported] The benefit of RAS blockade on kidney failure and survival is reported to be greatest when treatment starts at the microscopic haematuria or microalbuminuria stage. - PMID:42316418

[B | evidence supported] In the EMPA-KIDNEY randomized trial, empagliflozin reduced kidney disease progression (HR 0.71), with no significant heterogeneity by primary kidney disease, including glomerular disease. However, enrolment required eGFR ≥20, so no randomized data apply at eGFR <15. - PMID:38061372

[B | evidence supported] EARLY PRO-TECT was under-enrolled relative to its protocol. The protocol planned about 120 children aged 24 months to 18 years, with up to 80 randomized. Only 66 oligosymptomatic children took part: 22 randomized and 44 in an open-arm comparison. - PMID:22811928, PMID:32299679
[B | evidence supported] Final safety result: ramipril caused no safety signal over 216.4 patient-years. The adverse event rate-ratio versus comparison was 1.00 (95% CI 0.66-1.53). - PMID:32299679

[B | evidence supported] In a meta-analysis of 267 male XLAS COL4A5 mutations, mutation type predicted age at end-stage renal failure. The groups were: truncating/large rearrangement/splice donor, mean 19.8±5.7 years; non-glycine or 3' glycine missense, in-frame indels and splice acceptor, mean 25.7±7.2 years; 5' glycine substitutions, mean 30.1±7.2 years. - PMID:12105244

[B | guideline supported] The 2024 ERKNet/ERA/ESPN guideline names early RAS blockade as standard of care and states SGLT2i may be added in adults with proteinuria and CKD. It also acknowledges that clinical trials in this disease are scarce and limited. - PMID:39673454

[C | evidence supported] In Alport syndrome, an adult-nephrology narrative review states that ACE inhibitors, or ARBs if ACE inhibitors are not tolerated, slow progression and can delay kidney failure by years. No numeric effect size is given in the source. - PMID:38745975

[C | emerging] In high-risk IgA nephropathy, control arms on maximally tolerated RAASi alone had a pooled annual eGFR slope of -4.5 mL/min/1.73m2. This shows a residual decline despite RAASi, in a different glomerular disease. - PMID:42584957

[C | emerging] In a single-centre retrospective cohort of 121 adults with non-diabetic CKD, finerenone initiation was associated with attenuation of eGFR decline (reported before–after slope improvement of 5.07 mL/min/1.73m2/yr). Hyperkalemia occurred in 4.96% of patients.

blocks.text: Across MRA RCTs, hyperkalemia and adverse events were more frequent at lower baseline eGFR. - PMID:42965115, PMID:42973695

items: [C | evidence supported] Urate-lowering therapy did not consistently change eGFR outcomes in CKD trials (CKD-FIX annual eGFR decline difference about -0.10 mL/min/1.73m2, non-significant). It is not supported solely for renoprotection. - PMID:42688589

[C | emerging] In IgA nephropathy trials, a treatment effect of approximately 30% proteinuria reduction predicted at least 90% probability of nonzero eGFR slope benefit. This supports proteinuria change as a surrogate input in slope models. - PMID:33775708

[C | evidence supported] The KFRE was validated across CKD stages 3-5 in a large multinational individual-participant meta-analysis. Discrimination was high (C 0.90 at 2 years, 0.88 at 5 years) and similar across age, race and diabetes subgroups. Stage-specific performance at eGFR <10-15 and performance by cause of CKD (including hereditary nephropathy) are not reported in the abstract. - PMID:26757465

[C | evidence supported] KFRE calibration is not uniform across populations. The original equations overestimated risk in some non-North American cohorts, and a regional calibration factor improved calibration. - PMID:26757465

[C | evidence supported] Single-country external validations confirmed excellent 2-year KFRE discrimination. However, these cohorts were older patients with moderate CKD, unlike this patient. - PMID:36529658, PMID:38405300

[C | emerging] In an advanced (predominantly G3b-G4) diabetic kidney disease cohort, static KFRE discrimination was markedly lower (C 0.689). Longitudinal creatinine and haematocrit trajectories added prognostic information beyond the KFRE. - PMID:42900647
[C | evidence supported] KFRE calibration is affected by competing mortality. In UK Biobank, kidney failure risk was underestimated in people with multimorbidity. - PMID:41288315

[C | evidence supported] The KFRE's stated clinical role is predicting kidney replacement therapy need, and it requires albuminuria as an input. Its use is framed around guiding referral timing and dialysis-access planning. - PMID:36529658

[C | evidence supported] Retrospective observational data are reported to show that ACE-inhibitor therapy, ramipril in particular, delays kidney failure (ESKD) and improves life expectancy in Alport patients with proteinuria. The magnitude of delay is not stated in any provided source. - PMID:22811928, PMID:35547199, PMID:40165927

[C | evidence supported] A 2025 systematic review of Alport management found that study heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis. This is consistent with the absence of a pooled numeric effect size in the provided sources. - PMID:40165927

[C | guideline supported] The patient's COL4A5 p.Gly1048Glu is classified as a VUS. Genomic reviews state that variants of uncertain significance should not independently determine treatment or donor eligibility. The clinical X-linked Alport diagnosis rests on phenotype and pedigree. - PMID:39673454, PMID:42792963

[C | emerging] Human evidence for SGLT2 inhibitors in Alport syndrome specifically is essentially absent from the major CKD trial data. DAPA-CKD included only a handful of Alport patients, and the authors state results cannot be extrapolated to Alport syndrome. - PMID:35547199

[C | hypothesis] A review argues that SGLT2i renal benefit may depend on BMI, with minimal or no benefit possible at BMI <25. It notes that Alport syndrome often affects lean individuals whose progression is not driven by hyperfiltration and volume mechanisms, so benefit in Alport syndrome remains uncertain. - PMID:40053507

[C | emerging] Recent reviews state that RAAS blockade remains the foundation of Alport treatment. They describe SGLT2i among adjunctive agents that may offer additional kidney protection, a statement of potential rather than demonstrated benefit. - PMID:32064497, PMID:41243004

[C | evidence supported] In broad CKD (EMPA-KIDNEY bioimpedance substudy), empagliflozin produced a sustained reduction in estimated fluid overload. This is one proposed mechanism of benefit, but it was not studied in Alport syndrome specifically. - PMID:38082486

[C | emerging] In a retrospective cohort of 1011 CKD patients already on an SGLT2 inhibitor whose eGFR progressed to ≤20 mL/min/1.73 m2, continuation (vs discontinuation) was associated with higher IPTW-adjusted 2-year dialysis-free survival (58.9% vs 41.7%) and patient survival (71.7% vs 40.6%). The authors note that evidence for continuation below eGFR 20 is otherwise limited. - PMID:42699509

[C | evidence supported] A narrative review states that SGLT2 inhibitor cardiorenal benefit in randomized trials extends down to eGFR 20 mL/min/1.73 m2, defining the lower limit of trial evidence. - PMID:42942386

[C | hypothesis] An early eGFR decline after SGLT2 inhibitor initiation is described as usually a functional hemodynamic response. In a heart-failure cohort, eGFR remained below pretreatment at 12 months after an early >10% decline. - PMID:42741732, PMID:42941673

[C | emerging] No provided source evaluates or validates the KFRE in Alport syndrome, other monogenic kidney diseases, or young adults. The only Alport-specific progression modelling found used urinary biomarkers, not KFRE. In 127 patients with Alport syndrome, UACR was independently associated with yearly eGFR loss after adjustment that included age, eGFR and mode of inheritance. The authors state this requires external validation. - PMID:42415835

[C | emerging] In autosomal dominant Alport syndrome due to monoallelic COL4A3 p.Gly407Arg, proteinuria ≥500 mg/g was associated with faster eGFR decline and renal events. This is an Alport-specific prognostic marker, but it is not a validation of KFRE. - PMID:41931366

[C | evidence supported] Retrospective observational data are reported to show that ACE-inhibitor therapy delays renal failure and improves life expectancy in Alport patients with proteinuria. The source gives no numeric delay, hazard ratio, or stage stratification. - PMID:22811928, PMID:35547199

[C | evidence supported] A 2025 systematic review of Alport management found that observational studies suggest early intervention might delay dialysis and improve life expectancy. Significant heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis, so no pooled effect size is available. - PMID:40165927

[C | evidence supported] Patients with Alport syndrome and chronically elevated albuminuria are described as being at high risk of kidney failure before age 50. This is relevant only as a qualitative natural-history anchor, not as a treatment effect size. - PMID:39122650

[C | evidence supported] Final efficacy result in the randomized arm: ramipril cut the risk of progression to the next disease level by almost half (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.12-2.20). This was not statistically significant. Ramipril also lessened the slope of albuminuria progression and the decline in GFR. - PMID:32299679

[C | evidence supported] Supportive analyses gave similar estimates. In adjusted analysis, open-label treated children versus untreated children showed HR 0.53 (0.22-1.29). A Bayesian synthesis combining the open-arm and randomized data gave HR 0.52 (0.19-1.39). - PMID:32299679

[C | evidence supported] An accompanying editorial judged the trial under-enrolled and not positive in the traditional sense. It nonetheless saw strong supportive evidence for long-term safety and for slowing albuminuria and eGFR decline with early ACE inhibition. - PMID:32444091

[C | evidence supported] A later analysis of 58 trial children used urine LCMS measurement to verify adherence. Confirmed ramipril record was high, at 96% and 95% at two time points. This supports the view that the trial results were not undermined by non-adherence. - PMID:41272348

[C | evidence supported] In a Danish cohort, collagenous-domain glycine substitutions were associated with an adult form of XLAS, mean age at ESRD 35.8 years. Truncating mutations had a mean of 21.6 years. The authors conclude the prognostic usefulness of COL4A5 mutation analysis is limited. - PMID:19728970

[C | evidence supported] In male XLAS (LOVD, n=157), COL4A5 glycine substitutions with a highly destabilising replacement residue were associated with a median age at kidney failure about 7 years earlier and hearing-loss diagnosis about 21 years earlier. Glycine substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region were associated with kidney failure about 19 years later. The source lists Glu among the highly destabilising residues. - PMID:35177655

[C | evidence supported] Severity in affected males correlated with the degree of predicted disruption of the α5 chain. The phenotype of an individual mutation was very consistent within families for deafness, lenticonus and timing of ESRF. - PMID:12105244, PMID:8651296
[C | emerging] The trial protocol expects most participants to be children with normal eGFR. This means any eventual results will mainly describe early-stage disease. - PMID:39122650

[C | emerging] A pediatric review notes that SGLT2i data in pediatric kidney disease are limited and that randomized trials are needed. This supports the view that disease-specific effect estimates are still lacking. - PMID:39950157

[D | hypothesis] In Col4a3 knockout Alport mice, dapagliflozin alone did not mitigate early functional decline or albuminuria. Combined with ramipril from 4 weeks of age, it improved renal function and histology and extended survival compared with ramipril alone. - PMID:40499560

[D | hypothesis] In a preclinical randomized study in Col4a3-deficient mice with established nephropathy, late-onset ramipril alone and ramipril plus empagliflozin gave similar survival benefit. Adding finerenone extended survival further. - PMID:37428955

[D | hypothesis] In a small predialysis CKD cohort, neither time-dependent SGLT2 inhibitor use nor ACE inhibitor/ARB use was significantly associated with major adverse kidney or cardiovascular events. The authors advise caution because exposure was limited. - PMID:42942488

[D | hypothesis] In a cell-based assay, α5(IV) glycine missense mutants associated clinically with proteinuria and early renal failure showed significantly reduced heterotrimer secretion. Mutants without early proteinuria resembled wild type. The authors suggest the assay may help distinguish pathogenic from non-pathogenic variants. - PMID:32405592

[D | emerging] The only Alport-specific human effect estimates in the sources come from a small retrospective study of 18 adults treated with RASi plus SGLT2i, compared against their own preceding period on RASi alone. It reported improved chronic eGFR slope and reduced proteinuria, and the authors call for prospective validation. - PMID:42006198

[D | hypothesis] In Col4a3 knockout mice, dapagliflozin added to ramipril preserved renal function and extended survival compared with ramipril alone, whereas dapagliflozin alone did not mitigate early disease. This is preclinical, hypothesis-level data only. - PMID:40499560

[E | emerging] The only Alport-specific randomized human SGLT2i study in the sources is a protocol with no reported results. DOUBLE PRO-TECT Alport is a placebo-controlled dapagliflozin trial in ages 10-39 on stable maximum RAS inhibition with UACR >500 mg/g in adults. Its primary outcome is change in albuminuria, and most participants are expected to have normal eGFR. - PMID:39122650

[E | hypothesis] DOUBLE PRO-TECT Alport is represented in the sources only by its protocol. It is a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled dapagliflozin trial with change in UACR as the primary endpoint. No efficacy or safety results are reported in the provided sources. - PMID:39122650
