[D | emerging] Under the ACMG/AMP framework, co-segregation and phenotype specificity (PP4) influence classification. In one COL4A3 splice variant, a discordant maternal phenotype precluded supportive co-segregation and nonspecific isolated hematuria precluded PP4, so the variant remained a VUS despite functional splicing evidence. - PMID:42936413

[C | emerging] The 2024 International Workshop highlighted genetic variant curation and the challenges of variant interpretation and misclassification, especially in non-European populations. - PMID:41853742

[C | emerging] Glycine substitutions in the Gly-Xaa-Yaa repeat of the collagenous domain are the most common class of COL4A5 variant in Alport syndrome cohorts. This is background prevalence information, not a classification criterion. - PMID:19728970, PMID:42552945

[D | hypothesis] Pathogenic COL4A5 Gly substitutions to highly destabilising residues are associated with earlier kidney failure and earlier hearing loss diagnosis in males. In autosomal dominant disease (COL4A3/COL4A4), the residues defined as highly destabilising include Glu. Gly substitutions adjacent to non-collagenous regions are associated with later kidney failure and are over-represented in gnomAD. These are genotype-phenotype associations, not ACMG/ClinGen criteria. - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] Not all COL4A5 glycine substitutions are severe. The European founder variant p.G624D is described as hypomorphic with mostly milder symptoms, so substitution class alone cannot be assumed to predict severity. - PMID:36553470

[C | emerging] Reassessing historical Alport-spectrum variant reports under ACMG criteria downgraded a meaningful share of variants to VUS. About a quarter of index cases had ambiguous results. Downgraded VUS cases had more limited phenotypes than non-downgraded cases, which had extrarenal manifestations. - PMID:41851263

[D | emerging] In published X-linked Alport families with novel COL4A5 variants, demonstrated co-segregation with affected relatives was used together with functional or tissue evidence to support pathogenicity. That evidence included minigene and in vivo transcript analysis and absent α5 chain staining in skin basement membrane. - PMID:31901041, PMID:34774011, PMID:42180677

[D | emerging] Variable expressivity, reduced penetrance and variable renal involvement in heterozygous carriers can complicate the interpretation of segregation in collagen IV nephropathy pedigrees. Affection status of relatives, especially female carriers, may not cleanly track genotype. - PMID:37761826, PMID:39911173, PMID:42881817

[D | hypothesis] In an adult with probable autosomal dominant Alport syndrome, a novel heterozygous COL4A4 missense variant met PM1, PM2 and PP3 under generic ACMG/AMP criteria. It remained classified as a VUS, although phenotype, ultrastructure and family history were considered supportive. - PMID:42774990

[C | emerging] In a Polish Alport cohort, COL4A3-5 variants were classified using generic ACMG/AMP guidelines. A recurrent COL4A5 glycine substitution (p.Gly624Asp) accounted for 31% of X-linked Alport syndrome cases. No gene-specific criterion weighting was described. - PMID:40004525

[C | evidence supported] The Alport variant consensus refines the ACMG criteria. It designates position-1 glycine residues in the Gly-X-Y repeats of the collagenous domain as mutational hotspots (PM1). In a population database, position-1 Gly substitutions were associated with haematuria. The consensus also notes that hypomorphic variants (often glycine near a non-collagenous interruption) complicate interpretation, and that most predicted pathogenic COL4A5 population variants had potentially mitigating features. - PMID:33854215, PMID:34400539

[D | emerging] In a regional pediatric cohort with COL4A3/4/5 testing, glycine-substituting missense variants were the most frequent molecular defect. Cascade testing identified additional genetically affected relatives in all tested families. The patient's variant (p.Gly1048Glu) is a glycine substitution, but the source does not state how this variant class maps to ACMG criteria such as PM1. - PMID:42552945

[C | evidence supported] Glycine substitutions account for nearly half of the pathogenic COL4A3-COL4A5 variants that cause Alport syndrome. This makes them the dominant pathogenic missense class, but the source does not describe a formal classification rule (e.g., PM1) for them. - PMID:35177655, PMID:42552945

[D | hypothesis] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome, COL4A5 glycine substitutions with a highly destabilising replacement residue were associated with an earlier median age at kidney failure and at hearing-loss diagnosis. Glutamate (Glu) is explicitly listed among the highly destabilising residues, in the analysis of COL4A3/COL4A4 heterozygotes. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] Not all COL4A5 glycine substitutions behave equally. Those adjacent to a non-collagenous region (interruption or terminus) were associated with later kidney failure, and COL4A5 variants adjacent to non-collagenous regions were over-represented in gnomAD. Position relative to interruptions is therefore relevant when weighing a glycine substitution. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] Individual COL4A5 glycine substitutions in the collagenous domain have been classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic in reported families: Gly545Ser (likely pathogenic by ACMG, segregating over three generations), Gly624Asp (pathogenic) and Gly775Val (pathogenic, de novo). - PMID:42255916, PMID:42881817, PMID:42905207

[C | emerging] Deafness and lenticonus are consistent within families for a given COL4A5 mutation. Knowing the genotype adds prognostic information on extrarenal disease. Non-glycine or 3' glycine missense variants were associated with fewer extrarenal symptoms. - PMID:12105244

[C | evidence supported] Molecular diagnosis can support safer assessment of living-related donors. However, a variant of uncertain significance should not by itself determine treatment or donor eligibility, and segregation and phenotype should be weighed. - PMID:42792963

[C | evidence supported] Genetic testing is described as the gold standard for diagnosing Alport syndrome and establishing its mode of inheritance. A narrative review cautions that variants of uncertain significance should not on their own determine treatment or donor eligibility, and should be evaluated against segregation and phenotype. - PMID:23349312, PMID:42792963

[D | emerging] COL4A5 defects account for most cases of post-transplant anti-GBM disease. Gene deletions are reported to be more commonly associated with the complication than point mutations. This implies, but does not quantify, lower risk for missense variants. - PMID:14717941

[C | emerging] Whole-exome sequencing of living donors found that 13.1% carried variants linked to latent renal or systemic conditions despite no clinical signs at donation. This indirectly supports genetic screening of related donor candidates. - PMID:41194031

[D | emerging] COL4A5 gene deletions are more commonly associated with post-transplant anti-GBM disease than point mutations. A small German series observed anti-GBM antibodies after transplant in patients with a deletion and a splice-site mutation. - PMID:1450636, PMID:14717941

[C | emerging] In a regional paediatric cohort tested for COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 with ACMG classification, glycine-substituting missense variants were the most frequent molecular defect (9/18). Cascade testing found additional genetically affected relatives in every family tested. - PMID:42552945

[D | hypothesis] Individual COL4A5 glycine substitutions have been reported as pathogenic: p.Gly624Asp was inherited from a hemizygous father with Alport syndrome, with familial segregation analysis performed, and p.Gly775Val arose de novo. p.Gly624Asp was described as usually associated with late-onset disease and variable renal involvement. - PMID:42881817, PMID:42905207

[E | hypothesis] The provided sources contain no report of COL4A5 p.Gly1048Glu (c.3143G>A). Its pathogenicity cannot be established from this evidence set. The general variant class is the most frequent pathogenic class in Alport syndrome: glycine substitutions in the Gly-Xaa-Yaa collagenous domain. - PMID:19728970, PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 glycine substitutions adjacent to non-collagenous regions are over-represented in the normal population (gnomAD). Proximity to an interruption is therefore relevant to how much weight a glycine VUS can be given toward pathogenicity. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] Variant type is the only genotype risk factor stated in the sources. COL4A5 gene deletions are more commonly associated with post-transplant anti-GBM disease than point mutations. No source specifically assesses glycine missense variants for this complication. - PMID:14717941

[C | emerging] In a WES cohort, 13.1% of living kidney donors carried variants associated with latent renal or systemic conditions despite no clinical manifestation at donation. This supports the potential value of genomic screening of donors. - PMID:41194031

[C | evidence supported] Expert consensus treats position-1 Gly residues of Gly-X-Y repeats in the intermediate collagenous domain as mutational hotspots (PM1). The same consensus notes that hypomorphic variants are often Gly residues adjacent to a non-collagenous interruption, which complicates benign-frequency thresholds. - PMID:33854215

[D | hypothesis] There is no ClinVar record of COL4A5 c.3143G>A / p.Gly1048Glu. The only missense variant at codon 1048 in ClinVar is c.3142G>A p.Gly1048Arg, classified as Uncertain significance with single-submitter review and linked to X-linked Alport syndrome. A same-codon pathogenic precedent, which could otherwise support classification, is therefore not available. - DB:05fe945e878922e0, DB:e50be02881e9e351

blocks.text: Verified research findings (106)

items: [B | evidence supported] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome, truncating-type COL4A5 mutations were associated with the earliest mean age at ESRF. 3' glycine missense variants fell into an intermediate group, and 5' glycine substitutions had the latest mean ESRF age. Glycine substitutions as a class therefore did not predict ESRF age comparably to truncating variants, although position modified severity. - PMID:12105244

[B | evidence supported] In a meta-analysis of male X-linked Alport genotype-phenotype data, mutation type significantly predicted age at end-stage renal failure. Truncating-type variants (large rearrangements, frameshift, nonsense, splice donor) had the earliest mean ESRF age (~19.8 y). 3' glycine/non-glycine missense variants were intermediate (~25.7 y) and 5' glycine substitutions were latest (~30.1 y). On average, glycine substitutions therefore carry later, not equivalent, kidney failure risk than truncating variants, with overlap given the standard deviations. - PMID:12105244

[B | evidence supported] Within families, the phenotype of an individual COL4A5 mutation was reported to be very consistent for deafness, lenticonus and timing of ESRF onset. This makes the family's age pattern of kidney failure informative for both variant interpretation and prognosis. - PMID:12105244

[C | evidence supported] COL4A5 encodes the α5(IV) chain. Together with α3 and α4 it forms a heterotrimer that is the major structural collagen of the GBM. Disruption of this heterotrimer is the structural basis on which a helix-destabilisation mechanism would act. - DB:310c87d59a4fb64f, PMID:39899372

[C | emerging] A genotype-focused review reports that in vitro studies suggest collagen IV missense variants cause impaired type IV collagen trafficking and ER stress. Unlike truncating variants in hemizygous males, missense variants still allow α3α4α5(IV) to be synthesised. This is consistent with a retention or misfolding mechanism rather than absent synthesis. - PMID:39899372

[C | emerging] In a pediatric X-linked Alport cohort, minigene assays showed that 10 of 26 intronic and exonic COL4A5 single-nucleotide variants caused aberrant mRNA splicing. Splicing abnormality was associated with faster eGFR decline. An apparent missense variant may therefore act partly through mis-splicing rather than, or in addition to, protein retention. - PMID:40567900

[C | evidence supported] Narrative reviews and a UniProt record state that pathogenic COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 variants cause absence or malfunction of the collagen IV α3α4α5 scaffold. This scaffold is described as an essential, major structural component of the GBM. Variants affecting these chains are stated to cause Alport syndrome and its variants. - DB:310c87d59a4fb64f, PMID:29673759, PMID:35283436

[C | evidence supported] A narrative review reports that de novo anti-GBM disease after kidney transplantation for Alport syndrome is a recognized phenomenon. Separately, a small case series reports generally favorable transplant outcomes in genetically confirmed Alport syndrome, alongside vascular and late antibody-mediated complications. - PMID:28515156, PMID:42076904

[C | hypothesis] Narrative reviews describe how Gly substitutions in the Gly-X-Y repeat cause triple-helix misfolding. They also describe reduced secretion with possible dominant-negative effects, and ER stress from misfolded matrix proteins, as general disease mechanisms. Collagen's nucleated-growth assembly makes it particularly vulnerable to structurally abnormal but partially functional chains. - PMID:2010058, PMID:30768852, PMID:38186852

[C | evidence supported] Within families, a given COL4A5 mutation showed a very consistent phenotype for deafness, lenticonus and timing of ESRF onset. This is relevant to interpreting concordant early kidney failure among maternal-line male relatives. - PMID:12105244

[C | emerging] On reassessment under ACMG criteria, COL4A3/4/5 variants downgraded to VUS were associated with more limited phenotypes (e.g., isolated microscopic hematuria) than non-downgraded cases with extrarenal manifestations. Genetic reports from the pre-ACMG era warrant critical re-evaluation. - PMID:41851263

[C | hypothesis] In autosomal dominant Alport syndrome (single COL4A3/COL4A4 variants), glycine substitutions in distal exons were associated with worse kidney survival than proximal ones, while severe (truncating-type) variants did not affect renal survival. This contrasts with the X-linked pattern. - PMID:39810285, PMID:42172079

[C | emerging] In a patient cohort study, some COL4A5 glycine substitutions were associated with absent immunological expression of α3(IV)–α5(IV) chains in the glomerular basement membrane. This is patient-tissue evidence of failed network deposition, though not direct proof of intracellular retention. - PMID:8940267

[C | hypothesis] A review states that in vitro studies of Alport missense variants suggest impaired type IV collagen trafficking and ER stress. It also states that α3α4α5(IV) is still synthesized with missense variants, in contrast to truncating variants in males. - PMID:39899372

[C | emerging] In a small Chinese cohort, COL4A5 glycine substitutions by an acidic amino acid were associated with more severe clinical manifestations than other missense mutations. The patient's p.Gly1048Glu is a glycine-to-acidic (glutamic acid) substitution. - PMID:28542346

[C | evidence supported] In a second cohort of male X-linked Alport patients, truncating variants also predicted earlier ESRD than non-truncating ones (mean 21.6 vs 33.1 years). Collagenous-domain glycine substitutions gave an adult form (mean ESRD 35.8 years). The author cautioned that genotype-phenotype correlations were not distinct enough to make COL4A5 results strongly predictive of prognosis. - PMID:19728970

[C | evidence supported] Glycine substitutions are not uniformly severe. For example, the European founder COL4A5 p.G624D is described as hypomorphic with mostly milder symptoms. Phenotypic severity of glycine variants therefore depends on the specific variant. - PMID:36553470

[C | emerging] Some COL4A5 variants annotated as missense or non-canonical intronic have been shown by RNA analysis to cause exon skipping or intron retention. Examples are c.2689G>C (p.Glu897Gln) and c.451A>G in urine mRNA, and the c.3374-3T>G minigene. Splice-altering variants are often missed by DNA-only testing, so a presumed missense VUS may act through aberrant splicing. - PMID:37441478, PMID:42404581, PMID:42614610

[C | evidence supported] Pediatric X-linked Alport cohorts in China and Italy reported glycine substitutions as the most common COL4A5 defect, and the Danish series found the same. Being common does not by itself indicate pathogenicity for any individual variant. - PMID:19728970, PMID:37097554

[C | evidence supported] Post-transplant anti-GBM disease is reported in about 5% of Alport syndrome patients overall. One older source reports an average of 6% among male X-linked patients after renal transplantation. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934, PMID:8918711

[C | emerging] COL4A5 defects account for most cases, with alpha5(IV) NC1 as the usual alloantigen in X-linked disease. Gene deletions are reported to be associated with this complication more often than point mutations. No source quantifies risk for missense or glycine-substitution variants. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934, PMID:8918711

[C | evidence supported] Mechanistically, alloantibodies arise against the alpha345(IV) collagen network present in the donor GBM but absent or reduced in the Alport kidney. Quaternary epitopes of alpha345NC1 hexamers appear to initiate the alloimmune response in X-linked Alport recipients. - PMID:12778332, PMID:23620401, PMID:42390934

[C | evidence supported] When post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis occurs, it is severe and often leads to graft loss. On first transplantation, graft failure usually occurs within weeks to months and not usually beyond the first year. Recurrence with accelerated loss is reported after retransplantation. Some patients develop anti-GBM antibodies without ever developing clinical nephritis. - PMID:14717941, PMID:42390934

[C | evidence supported] There is no agreed protocol for prophylaxis or treatment of post-transplant anti-GBM nephritis in Alport syndrome. Even so, kidney transplantation is described as an effective treatment for Alport syndrome when guided by molecular confirmation and careful donor evaluation. - PMID:16911486, PMID:42076904, PMID:42390934

[C | emerging] An older meta-analysis of 267 male COL4A5 mutations reported a positional gradient. 5' glycine substitutions had a later mean ESRF age (30.1 years) than 3' glycine missense mutations (grouped with other non-truncating variants, 25.7 years). The intrafamilial phenotype of an individual mutation was very consistent for timing of ESRF, deafness and lenticonus. - PMID:12105244

[C | emerging] In a Danish cohort, collagenous-domain glycine substitutions were associated with an adult form (mean ESRD 35.8 years) versus 21.6 years for truncating mutations. The author concluded that genotype-phenotype correlations for non-truncating variants were not clear-cut and that their prognostic usefulness was limited. - PMID:19728970

[C | evidence supported] Protein-level evidence: absence of the alpha5(IV) chain on basement-membrane immunostaining (e.g., skin biopsy) supports a diagnosis of X-linked Alport syndrome. This is a tissue-based functional readout available in addition to sequencing. - PMID:19728970

[C | emerging] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome, COL4A5 glycine substitutions by a highly destabilising residue were associated with earlier kidney failure (median about 7 years earlier) and earlier hearing-loss diagnosis (about 21 years earlier). The authors conclude that the nature of the substitution and of nearby residues helps determine risk of early kidney failure. - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] The residues classed as highly destabilising (Arg, Val, Glu, Asp, Trp) were defined in the context of heterozygous COL4A3/COL4A4 variants, where they were associated with increased haematuria risk. Glu is explicitly in this class. - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] Position relative to non-collagenous regions also modified outcome. COL4A5 Gly substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region were associated with kidney failure about 19 years later, and exon location had no effect. - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] Older male cohort data support a general correlation between the degree of predicted alpha5 chain disruption and phenotype severity. Missense variants as a group were associated with better renal survival than other variant types. - PMID:38790222, PMID:8651296

[C | emerging] In a genotype-phenotype analysis of COL4A5 Gly substitutions in males with X-linked Alport syndrome, location was categorised by exon (exons 1-20 versus exon 21 to the carboxyl terminus). Variants were also classified by adjacency to a non-collagenous region (interruption or terminus) and by the destabilising effect of the replacement residue. The abstract reports that exon location had no effect. That sentence follows the autosomal dominant COL4A3/COL4A4 haematuria analysis, so whether it also applies to kidney-failure age in COL4A5 males is not explicit in the abstract. - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] COL4A5 Gly substitutions with a highly destabilising replacement residue were associated with a 7-year earlier median age at kidney failure and a 21-year earlier age at hearing-loss diagnosis in males. In the same study, Glu is named among the highly destabilising residues (listed in the COL4A3/COL4A4 analysis). - PMID:35177655

[C | emerging] COL4A5 Gly substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region (an interruption of the collagenous domain or a terminus) were associated with kidney failure delayed by 19 years. Such variants were also over-represented in the general population (gnomAD). - PMID:35177655

[C | hypothesis] Exonic substitutions in COL4A5 can cause aberrant splicing. Splicing variants account for about 15% of X-linked Alport cases, and in-frame versus out-of-frame splicing outcomes differ in kidney survival. cDNA, minigene or urine-cell RNA analysis can determine the effect. - PMID:35211492

[C | evidence supported] Segregation is listed alongside gene-disease validity, inheritance, molecular mechanism and phenotype as a required dimension of variant evaluation in inherited kidney disease. VUS should not independently determine treatment or living-related donor eligibility. The source gives no quantitative weighting for segregation. - PMID:42792963

[C | evidence supported] In a large genetic eye-disorder cohort, VUS were reassessed using segregation studies, literature/database review and bioinformatic tools. Variant reclassification produced 39 additional diagnoses, though some phenotype-consistent VUS still could not be reclassified. This shows segregation can contribute to resolving VUS, but its separate contribution is not reported. - PMID:41615371

[C | evidence supported] In skin biopsy series of suspected or confirmed X-linked Alport syndrome, α5(IV) staining of the epidermal basement membrane is typically absent in affected males and segmental or mosaic in females. - PMID:10200983, PMID:17554254, PMID:22921432

[C | evidence supported] Normal α5(IV) staining does not exclude a COL4A5 mutation. A substantial minority of patients, including at least one with a COL4A5 missense variant, retain the mutant protein in basement membranes with a normal staining pattern. - PMID:10200983, PMID:17554254, PMID:22921432

[C | emerging] In males with genetically confirmed X-linked Alport syndrome, positive kidney α5(IV) staining was seen in about 15 of 52 patients (over 20%). It was almost entirely limited to non-truncating variants (missense, in-frame deletions, in-frame splice) or somatic mosaicism. No truncating variant appeared in the positive group. This is the only source information comparing staining by variant class. It does not address skin staining, reduced versus mosaic patterns, or glycine substitutions as a separate group. - PMID:24304881

[C | emerging] Missense variants in the α5(IV)-positive group were more likely to lie before exon 25 than missense variants in the α5(IV)-negative group. This implies that missense variants, depending on location, can give either positive or absent staining. - PMID:24304881

[C | emerging] Retained α5(IV) staining was associated with significantly lower urinary protein and later onset of end-stage kidney disease than absent staining. This is an association, not proof that staining causes or predicts outcome in an individual patient. - PMID:24304881

[C | emerging] Consensus criteria treat position-1 glycines of the Gly-X-Y repeats in the intermediate collagenous domain as mutational hotspots (PM1). They note that hypomorphic variants are often glycines adjacent to a non-collagenous interruption. Whether Gly1048 sits next to an interruption is therefore relevant to variant interpretation, but this source does not say where Gly1048 lies. - PMID:33854215

[C | emerging] Sequencing and minigene assays are commonly used to confirm splicing variants in COL4A3-5. Formal functional assays (PS3/BS3) remain mainly research tools. An example: a COL4A3 canonical splice variant was assessed with SpliceAI, Pangolin and MaxEntScan, then minigenes, which showed complete in-frame exon skipping. No source reports such an assessment for COL4A5 c.3143G>A. - PMID:33854215, PMID:42936413

[C | emerging] Methods beyond exome sequencing, including RNA-seq, resolved additional Alport cases with noncoding, copy-number or structural variants. Transcript-level analysis can therefore reveal effects that DNA sequencing alone does not. - PMID:41872207

[D | hypothesis] In contrast to protein-truncating variants in males with X-linked Alport syndrome, missense variants still permit α3α4α5(IV) synthesis. In vitro studies suggest missense variants cause impaired collagen IV trafficking and ER stress. This is compatible with a misfolding mechanism, which could include triple-helix destabilisation, but the sources do not directly demonstrate helix destabilisation. - PMID:39899372

[D | hypothesis] The only structural or molecular-dynamics analysis in the source set concerns a COL4A3 in-frame exon-skipping variant that preserves the Gly-X-Y register. The authors considered the simulations hypothesis-generating and not evidence of altered stability. No source provides direct experimental helix-stability data for COL4A5 glycine substitutions. - PMID:42936413

[D | hypothesis] In human undifferentiated podocytes, overexpressed COL4A3 chains were retained in the ER, with activation of unfolded protein response markers. Normal and mutant (G1334E) chains activated the UPR differently. Similar findings were seen in a Col4a3-G1332E knock-in mouse with an Alport-like phenotype and in biopsies from TBMN patients heterozygous for COL4A3-G1334E. - PMID:24262798

[D | hypothesis] In a female Col4a5+/- mouse and in Col4a5+/- podocytes, Col4a5 knockdown directly induced ER stress. Triptolide/Minnelide raised Col4a5 expression and reduced ER stress and proteinuria in mice. This ties COL4A5 loss to podocyte ER stress, but through reduced expression rather than retention of a misfolded missense chain. - PMID:41737559

[D | hypothesis] A review of Alport treatment approaches lists chaperone therapy among candidate strategies. This implies that protein misfolding and trafficking defects are considered a plausible therapeutic target, but the abstract gives no supporting data. - PMID:40938675

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 encodes the collagen α5(IV) chain. It is a secreted basement-membrane protein, and type IV collagen is the major structural component of the glomerular basement membrane. Defective secretion would therefore plausibly reduce α5(IV) in the GBM. - DB:310c87d59a4fb64f

[D | hypothesis] In CRISPR knock-in mouse models carrying human XLAS truncating Col4a5 variants (K229X, R471X), hemizygous males lost α5(IV) at mRNA/protein level. They developed irregular GBM thickening with lamination, hematuria, proteinuria and age-progressive glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis. R471X mice reached end-stage kidney disease at a median of 28 weeks. This is direct experimental support for α5 network deficiency causing the GBM lesion and progressive kidney failure. - PMID:30582011, PMID:42303719

[D | hypothesis] In a human mother–son case with a COL4A5 glycine missense variant (p.Gly1170Ser) in a G-X-Y repeat, COL4A5 immunolabeling was reduced only in Bowman's capsule despite distorted GBM ultrastructure. Superimposed segmental IgA deposition was also present. The authors suggest missense variants may affect collagen assembly differently by compartment, so the GBM α5 network may not be visibly absent. - PMID:38668984

[D | emerging] Functional validation (a minigene splicing assay) was used to establish pathogenicity of a novel COL4A5 non-canonical splice variant. The authors stress that functional validation is needed for uncertain variant types. - PMID:42404581

[D | hypothesis] Reviews state that current therapy is limited to ACE inhibition to slow progression. Approaches to replace or restore the α3α4α5 scaffold (gene editing, RNA splicing interference, translational control) are in development, with no clinical efficacy data in the sources. - PMID:35283436

[D | hypothesis] In a HEK293T cell-based screen, knockdown of cyclophilins showed that PPIF/cyclophilin D was involved in the ability of CsA and alisporivir to increase secretion of mutant α345(IV) collagen trimers. This links PPIF to the trimerization/secretion defect underlying Alport syndrome. - PMID:37143203

[D | hypothesis] Alisporivir, which binds cyclophilin but not calcineurin, increased secretion of mutant α345(IV) trimers, and other α345(IV) mutants were also responsive. The authors propose it as a candidate, not a validated therapy. - PMID:37143203
[D | hypothesis] The same source notes that CsA was previously reported to improve proteinuria in Alport syndrome but is not recommended because of nephrotoxicity. - PMID:37143203

[D | hypothesis] UniProt annotates PPIF as a mitochondrial peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase that may assist protein folding and is involved in regulating the mitochondrial permeability transition pore. This is consistent with a possible role in protein folding/secretion and in cell death pathways. - DB:ae219674a691ac62

[D | hypothesis] In diabetic nephropathy kidney transcriptomic datasets, PPIF was identified as a down-regulated mitochondrial/ER-stress-related gene. This is an associative finding in a different kidney disease, not Alport syndrome. - PMID:40775242

[D | hypothesis] Curated database annotation: EIF2AK3/PERK is a stress-sensing kinase. It recognises misfolded proteins, phosphorylates eIF2-alpha and triggers the integrated stress response, including preferential translation of ATF4. This is general protein biology and is not specific to COL4A5 or Alport syndrome. - DB:d48baf0a62ee1cab

[D | hypothesis] In ischemia-reperfusion acute kidney injury, transcriptomic analyses prioritised a PERK-ATF4-CHOP stress-apoptosis disease profile in injured proximal tubule cells. The authors explicitly say this suggests pathway engagement rather than causality. In pigs, a PERK/CHOP decrease accompanied lower early injury with dl-3-n-butylphthalide. - PMID:42328631

[D | hypothesis] In an in vitro study, cultured human podocytes showed elevated Sirt2 expression and high HDAC6 levels, with a reported Sirt2-HDAC6 regulatory complex. The study context was diabetic nephropathy, not Alport syndrome or COL4A5 disease. - PMID:42153196

[D | hypothesis] Per UniProt, HDAC6 transports misfolded proteins to the aggresome for autophagic clearance and is required for cilia disassembly via alpha-tubulin deacetylation. Whether misfolded mutant collagen IV alpha5 chains are handled by HDAC6 is untested in the provided sources. It is a hypothesis only. - DB:a92472f5874922af

[D | hypothesis] EDNRA encodes the endothelin-1 receptor (ET-A). It signals via G proteins that activate a phosphatidylinositol-calcium second messenger system. It binds endothelin-1 and endothelin-2 with higher affinity than endothelin-3. This is general receptor biology only. The source does not connect it to COL4A5, the glomerular basement membrane or Alport syndrome. - DB:4a397f2790c30f86

[D | hypothesis] SLC5A2 encodes SGLT2, a sodium-coupled glucose cotransporter. Its annotated primary role is reabsorbing D-glucose from glomerular filtrate in the early proximal tubule, so its kidney action is tubular, not in the glomerular basement membrane. The source draws no connection to COL4A5 or Alport syndrome. - DB:b661ab765bcc9c38

[D | hypothesis] In recombinant collagen-like proteins containing α5(IV) sequences, three Alport-associated Gly missense substitutions reduced thermal stability (lower melting temperature and calorimetric enthalpy). They also increased susceptibility to trypsin and chymotrypsin through local unwinding and abolished or greatly reduced integrin binding. - PMID:32085975

[D | hypothesis] A COL4A5 fragment carrying a Gly→Val substitution from an X-linked Alport patient, expressed in E. coli, showed altered circular dichroism spectra and secondary structure compared with control. The authors speculate that folding of the whole α5 chain may be affected. - PMID:15100740

[D | hypothesis] A mouse knock-in Gly→Glu substitution in the collagenous domain of Col4a3 (p.Gly1332Glu) reproduced key Alport features: about 30-35% shorter lifespan, proteinuria, raised urea and creatinine, and the typical basement-membrane changes. Mutant and normal α4/α5 chains appeared to be cleaved at or near the mutation site. - PMID:33718859

[D | hypothesis] A comparison of observed disease-causing Gly substitutions with expected rates found that the residues replacing Gly in α5(IV) are not randomly distributed. The authors argue that the degree of triple-helix destabilisation, rather than chemical dissimilarity, determines clinical outcome. Glu-specific underrepresentation was reported for α1(I), not for α5(IV). - PMID:15365990

[D | hypothesis] Other COL4A5 glycine substitutions are reported in X-linked Alport families: Gly325Arg in an adult-type kindred and Gly1196Glu in a heterozygous woman whose mother and two brothers had kidney failure. For Gly325Arg, effects on triple-helix formation were presumed rather than measured. - PMID:1376965, PMID:41799611

[D | hypothesis] Kidney transcriptome sequencing identified splice-altering variants, including noncanonical events, that routine DNA sequencing does not readily resolve across the Alport spectrum. This is a possible adjunct for clarifying variant consequence. - PMID:42614610

[D | hypothesis] In a cell-based split-nanoluciferase α345(IV) heterotrimer assay, COL4A5 glycine-substitution mutants associated clinically with proteinuria and early-onset renal failure all showed significantly reduced heterotrimer secretion. One showed poor intracellular trimer formation and the others showed low-level secretion. This is direct in vitro evidence of a secretion defect for α5-chain glycine substitutions. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] In the same assay, most glycine-substitution mutants from patients without proteinuria at a young age had trimer formation and secretion similar to wild type. Secretion defects therefore vary between glycine substitutions and appeared to track clinical severity. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] The authors propose that the heterotrimer formation/secretion assay may help distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic COL4A5 missense variants. An assay of this kind could serve as a source of functional evidence for a VUS. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] In a recombinant protein study, two glycine substitutions in the same α5(IV) domain (G1015V, juvenile-onset; G1030S, adult-onset) produced distinctly different secondary structures. This is structural, not secretion, evidence that glycine substitutions near residue 1048 can differ in effect. - PMID:15044104

[D | hypothesis] Among COL4A5 glycine substitutions in males, replacement by a highly destabilising residue was associated with a 7-year earlier median age at kidney failure and much earlier hearing loss. Substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous interruption delayed kidney failure by 19 years. Glu is named among the highly destabilising residues, but the abstract lists that set only in the COL4A3/COL4A4 heterozygous analysis. Exon location had no effect. - PMID:35177655

[D | emerging] Absence of the α5(IV) chain in epidermal basement membrane supports a diagnosis of X-linked Alport syndrome. In one family, a male with a COL4A5 glycine substitution (p.Gly1264Asp) had negative α5(IV) EBM staining. The sources contain no systematic comparison of α5 immunostaining patterns between glycine-substitution and truncating variants. - PMID:19728970, PMID:32328471

[D | hypothesis] In a cell-based assay of 9 COL4A5 glycine missense mutants, trimer secretion was significantly reduced in all mutants clinically associated with early proteinuria and early renal failure. Mutants without early proteinuria behaved closer to wild type. This suggests that defective α345(IV) network assembly may track with clinical severity. - PMID:32405592

[D | emerging] Standard anti-GBM ELISA can be negative in Alport post-transplant anti-GBM disease. Western blotting and alpha345NC1-hexamer-based immunoassays are described as more sensitive and specific. - PMID:14717941, PMID:23620401

[D | hypothesis] In a HEK293T cell reporter system, alisporivir, which binds cyclophilin but not calcineurin, increased secretion of mutant α345(IV) trimers. Other α345(IV) mutants also responded. - PMID:37143203

[D | hypothesis] Knockdown experiments implicated PPIF/cyclophilin D in the increase in mutant trimer secretion produced by cyclosporin A and alisporivir. This identifies a candidate mechanism, not a demonstrated therapeutic effect. - PMID:37143203

[D | hypothesis] The study authors report that cyclosporin A has been reported to improve proteinuria in Alport syndrome but is not recommended because of nephrotoxicity. They present alisporivir only as a possibly safer option, not a proven one. - PMID:37143203

[D | hypothesis] A narrative review states that proof-of-concept treatment strategies for basement-membrane collagen mutations have been developed in animal models. It does not identify alisporivir or cyclophilin D inhibition among them. - PMID:31387942

[D | hypothesis] In a transgenic mouse carrying a COL4A3 glycine substitution (p.G799R), the chemical chaperone TUDCA reduced ER stress, promoted secretion of mutant α3(IV) chains and improved kidney function. This is preclinical evidence in a different collagen IV gene, not COL4A5. - PMID:38782199

[D | hypothesis] Among COL4A5 glycine-substitution missense mutants tested in a cell-based assay, significantly reduced trimer secretion tracked with clinical severity (proteinuria, early kidney failure). The underlying defect differed: one mutant mainly failed at intracellular trimer formation, the others mainly at secretion. This heterogeneity implies that responsiveness to secretion-promoting interventions may be variant-specific, though no enhancer was tested. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] A cell-based α345(IV) heterotrimer formation and secretion assay largely correlated with clinical genotype–phenotype. It was proposed as a way to help distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic variants. Such an assay could in principle inform VUS interpretation for p.Gly1048Glu. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] Mouse models of Alport syndrome reproduce several features of the human disease and are considered useful for finding new treatments. However, their phenotype varies with genetic background and with the position and type of the alteration, which limits extrapolation of animal treatment responses to specific human variants. - PMID:36292778

[D | hypothesis] A review of genotype-based mechanisms reports that in vitro studies suggest missense variants in type IV collagen genes impair collagen trafficking and cause ER stress. In contrast, truncating variants act mainly through absence of the α3α4α5(IV) network. This gives a general mechanistic rationale for ER stress in missense Alport variants. It is not specific to COL4A5 glycine substitutions and does not name the PERK/CHOP pathway. - PMID:39899372

[D | hypothesis] In cultured podocytes, mutant COL4A3 chains were retained relative to wild type, and the UPR cascade was activated differentially. This is direct cell-level evidence of collagen IV retention and UPR activation for COL4A3 variants, not COL4A5. The abstract does not identify which UPR branch (PERK, IRE1, ATF6) or whether CHOP was involved. - PMID:25514610

[D | hypothesis] In a knock-in mouse carrying a COL4A3 glycine substitution (p.G799R), mutant α3 chains accumulated in the ER with defective secretion, causing persistent ER stress in vivo and in vitro. The key downstream mediator identified by RNA-seq was the MyD88/p38 MAPK pathway driving inflammation and apoptosis, not PERK/CHOP per the abstract. - PMID:38782199

[D | hypothesis] In the same mouse model, the chemical chaperone tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) reduced ER stress, promoted α3 secretion and improved kidney function. The authors suggest possible early clinical use, but this is preclinical only and not a treatment recommendation. - PMID:38782199

[D | hypothesis] A review proposes that HDACs promote renal fibrosis through non-histone epigenetic modifications. It suggests HDAC inhibitors as a possible tool to slow renal fibrosis in CKD generally. This is not specific to Alport or COL4A5 disease. - PMID:36148005

[D | hypothesis] A review reports protective effects of HDAC inhibitors in CKD, AKI, ADPKD and diabetic kidney disease. These include modulation of apoptosis, autophagy, inflammation and fibrosis. The same review states that selectivity, toxicity, drug resistance and pharmacokinetics remain unresolved. Alport syndrome is not among the diseases discussed. - PMID:40263937

[D | hypothesis] In males with X-linked Alport syndrome (Leiden Open Variation Database), COL4A5 Gly substitutions to a highly destabilising residue were associated with a 7-year reduction in median age at kidney failure and a 21-year reduction in age at hearing-loss diagnosis. In the same study's COL4A3/COL4A4 analysis, Glu is listed among the highly destabilising residues. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 Gly substitutions adjacent to a non-collagenous region (interruption or terminus) were associated with kidney failure about 19 years later and were over-represented in gnomAD. Exon location (exons 1-20 vs 21 to carboxyl terminus) had no effect on outcome. - PMID:35177655

[D | hypothesis] No source reports COL4A5 secretion or trimer-assembly assays for glycine substitutions. The only in vitro functional data concern a COL4A3 variant in HEK293T cells (reduced mRNA, weakened migration). Kidney transcriptome sequencing is reported to aid interpretation of splice-altering variants in the Alport spectrum. - PMID:42326388, PMID:42614610

[D | emerging] In a small single-centre adult cohort with mixed COL4A3/4/5 variants, missense variants were associated with better renal survival than other variant types. Median renal survival across the cohort was 42 years. - PMID:38790222

[D | emerging] In two families with suspected Alport syndrome carrying non-canonical COL4A5 splice-site variants, pathogenicity was clarified by combining several lines of evidence. These were familial co-segregation with comprehensive phenotyping of relatives, kidney-biopsy immunofluorescence showing aberrant collagen IV α5 staining, and minigene splicing assays showing exon 18 skipping. - PMID:41090128

[D | hypothesis] Computational assessments placed some VUS in functionally critical domains with predicted structural disruption. This was presented as supporting biological plausibility only. In the same cohort, Alport-group variants were confined to COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5, with pathogenicity correlating with severity and extrarenal manifestations. - PMID:41901018

[D | hypothesis] A cell-based α345(IV) heterotrimer formation/secretion assay has been applied to 9 COL4A5 glycine-substitution missense mutants. Reduced trimer secretion was seen in all mutants associated with proteinuria and early-onset renal failure, and results largely correlated with clinical genotype-phenotype. The abstract does not identify which residues were tested, so it cannot confirm whether p.Gly1048Glu or a nearby glycine substitution was studied. - PMID:32405592

[D | hypothesis] In population sequencing data, COL4A3-COL4A5 variants causing position-1 glycine substitutions in the collagen repeat were associated with hematuria. Most predicted pathogenic COL4A5 variants carried a biochemical feature that may mitigate clinical effect. Whether Gly1048 is a position-1 Gly and whether Glu lacks such mitigating features is not addressed in the sources. - PMID:34400539

[D | emerging] Preserved α3–α5(IV) expression has been reported in patients with progressive renal disease (thin or lamellated GBM variants). Absent expression was seen with wide, lamellated GBM diagnostic of Alport nephritis. Normal staining therefore did not equate to benign disease in this small series. - PMID:12203217

[D | hypothesis] COL4A5 has a triple-helical collagenous domain interrupted 22 times by non-collagenous sequences. Older case reports locate specific glycine substitutions between named interruptions: Gly325 between 4 and 5, Gly852 between 16 and 17, and Gly1143 between 19 and 20. Gly1048 is not mapped in any source. - PMID:1376965, PMID:7969679, PMID:8893151

[D | hypothesis] Glycine substitutions in the α5(IV) Gly-X-Y repeat are proposed to create an additional interruption and alter triple-helix formation. The same Gly1143Ser substitution produced variable renal-failure onset among relatives. - PMID:1376965, PMID:7969679

[D | emerging] In a literature review of Chinese males with X-linked Alport syndrome, COL4A5 deletion variants were associated with more frequent progression to ESRD than missense variants (36.0% vs 15.4%). This indirectly supports the stage note's premise that a truncating-like effect would matter prognostically. - PMID:33748275
